# Anthropic

The following Anthropic models are available in Amazon Bedrock:

Model | Description 
---|---
Claude Fable 5.2 | Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic's frontier model for technical work, setting a new bar in coding, finance, and the sciences. 
Claude Mythos 5.2 | Claude Mythos 5.2 is Anthropic's frontier model for cybersecurity and life sciences research, available through Anthropic's verification programs. 
Claude Haiku 5.5 | Claude Haiku 5.5 is the fastest and most efficient model in the Claude 5.5 family, built for high-volume, latency-sensitive work. It's the most capable Haiku model yet, with a clear step up over Claude Haiku 4.5 on coding and agent tasks. 
Claude Sonnet 5.5 | Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a smarter, more efficient Sonnet. It's a clear leap forward from Sonnet 5 on coding and knowledge work, at a much lower cost per task. 
Claude Opus 5.5 | Claude Opus 5.5 is Anthropic's most capable Opus model. Better at coding, knowledge work, and long-running tasks. It's easier to collaborate with and more cost efficient than ever. 
Claude Fable 5.1 | Claude Fable 5.1 is Anthropic's frontier model for ambitious coding, long-horizon agents, and enterprise knowledge work. 
Claude Mythos 5.1 | Claude Mythos 5.1 is Anthropic's most capable model for cybersecurity defense and life sciences research, including threat intelligence, vulnerability discovery, red teaming, drug discovery, and biodefense screening. 
Claude Opus 5 | Claude Opus 5 is Anthropic's most advanced Opus model, powering long-running agents while delivering improvements in coding and professional work. 
Claude Sonnet 5 | Claude Sonnet 5 is Anthropic's most capable Sonnet model yet, built for coding, agents, and professional work at scale. 
Claude Mythos 5 | Claude Mythos 5 is Anthropic's most capable model for cybersecurity and life sciences, including vulnerability discovery, drug design, and biodefense screening. 
Claude Fable 5 | Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's next-generation model for complex knowledge work and coding, capable of sustained autonomous operation across multi-day tasks. 
Claude Opus 4.8 | Claude Opus 4.8 is an Anthropic Opus model optimized for coding, agents, and deeper reasoning in enterprise workflows. 
Claude Opus 4.7 | Claude Opus 4.7 is an Anthropic Opus model built for coding, enterprise workflows, and long-running agentic tasks. 
Claude Sonnet 4.6 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 is a full upgrade of Anthropic's mid-tier model with improved coding, computer use, long-context reasoning, and agent planning with a 1M token context window. 
Claude Opus 4.6 | Claude Opus 4.6 is Anthropic's flagship model that plans more carefully, sustains agentic tasks longer, and operates reliably in massive codebases. 
Claude Opus 4.5 | Claude Opus 4.5 is Anthropic's model for coding, agents, and computer use with improvements for spreadsheets and long-running chats. 
Claude Haiku 4.5 | Claude Haiku 4.5 is Anthropic's lightweight model optimized for speed and efficiency with strong coding and agent performance. 
Claude Sonnet 4.5 | Claude Sonnet 4.5 is Anthropic's model optimized for agents, coding, and computer use with significant improvements across all benchmarks. 
Claude Opus 4.1 | Claude Opus 4.1 is an upgrade to Anthropic's model with improved coding, reasoning, and agentic task capabilities. 
Claude Sonnet 4 | Claude Sonnet 4 is Anthropic's balanced model with strong coding and reasoning capabilities, improved instruction following, and extended thinking with tool use. 
Claude 3 Haiku | Claude 3 Haiku is Anthropic's fastest and most compact Claude 3 model, optimized for speed and efficiency in near-instant responses. 

## Billing notes

The following billing behaviors apply specifically to Anthropic models on Amazon Bedrock:

Refused requests – A refused request returns HTTP 200 withstop_reason: "refusal". Whether it's billed depends on when the refusal occurred and on stop_details.category. These rules apply on both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints.

The following table describes eachstop_details.category value and whether Amazon Bedrock bills a refusal in that category before any output.

stop_details.category | What it means | Billed before any output 
---|---|---
"cyber" | The request could enable cyber harm, such as malware or exploit development. Benign cybersecurity work can also trigger this category. | No 
"bio" | The request could enable biological harm, such as dangerous lab methods. Beneficial life sciences work can also trigger this category. | Yes 
"frontier_llm" | The request could help with the development of competing AI models, which is restricted under Anthropic's commercial terms. Benign machine learning work can also trigger this category. | Yes 
"reasoning_extraction" | The request asks the model to reproduce its internal reasoning in the response text. To get reasoning in a structured form instead, use adaptive thinking. This category has no recommended fallback model, so change the prompt instead of retrying on another model. | Yes 
"general_harms" | The request falls under a usage-policy area outside the four named categories. Benign work can also trigger this category. | No 
null | The refusal doesn't map to a named category. null is a valid final value, not a placeholder. | No 

Amazon Bedrock bills a refusal before any output like any other request, at the refused model's rates. For a refusal that arrives mid-stream, after partial output, Amazon Bedrock bills the input tokens and the output tokens already streamed, in any category. Treat any partial output as incomplete and discard it.

In every case, the response'susage still reports token counts, and the request counts against your quotas. The set of billed categories can change.

## Model Details

Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic's frontier model for technical work, setting a new bar in coding, finance, and the sciences. Fable 5.2 takes on ambiguous problems for days, questions and verifies its own work, and orchestrates subagents to optimize results in a loop.

- Sampling parameters: temperature must be 1.0 or unset; top_p must be 0.99 or unset; temperature and top_p cannot be specified together; top_k is not supported
- Reasoning: Supported (adaptive thinking is always on and cannot be disabled; effort level configurable — low, medium, high, xhigh, max; default: high) See Adaptive thinking.

## Content Restrictions

Claude Fable 5.2 includes safety classifiers that block high-risk cybersecurity activities and most research biology tasks. When a classifier blocks a request, the API returns a standard HTTP 200 response withstop_reason: "refusal" and a stop_details object containing the restriction category. Organizations working in these areas can apply for less restrictive access through Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program and Life Sciences Verification Program.

Customers should handlestop_reason: "refusal" as a primary response path. Whether a refused request is billed depends on its category and on whether output had started. For details, see Billing notes.

Fallback credit for refused requests (beta)

When Claude Fable 5.2 refuses a request, the response can include a fallback credit token. Redeem the token when you retry the same request on a fallback model, and the retry is billed for the cached conversation prefix at cache-read rates instead of cache-write rates. Not every refusal carries a token. For more information, see Fallback credit for refused requests (beta).

Anthropic.content:
Compare which Claude Code features work on each Anthropic subscription plan, the Anthropic Console, and cloud providers such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud.

The Claude Code CLI and everything that runs locally work on every provider. For setup instructions per provider, see the Enterprise deployment overview. To skip straight to what is missing on your provider, see the summary by provider tabs.In the tables below, ✓ means available, ✗ means not available, and “See note” links to a footnote for partial support. A qualifier after ✓ narrows availability to that subset, and “Admin-enabled” means the feature is off until an organization admin turns it on.

Availability by model provider

How you authenticate determines which features Claude Code can reach. For a single list of what is missing on your provider, see the summary by provider tabs. To find your column in the tables:

Claude subscription: you sign in with a claude.ai account on the Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, or Enterprise plan

MCP servers: connectors from claude.ai load only when your claude.ai subscription is the active authentication method. Tool search isn’t supported on Microsoft Foundry deployments hosted on Azure. On Google Cloud (Google managed), tool search isn’t supported on models earlier than Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Haiku 4.5

Subagents: when the parent conversation runs Fable, the built-in Explore subagent runs on Opus with a Claude subscription, an Anthropic Console account, or an LLM gateway reached through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. On other providers, including Claude Platform on AWS, it runs on Fable

1 On Google Cloud (Google managed), web search is available for Opus 4, Sonnet 4, Haiku 4.5, and later models. 2 On these providers, auto mode supports only Claude Sonnet 5 or later, Opus 4.7 or later, Haiku 5.5, and the Fable models. See Auto mode configuration. For the permission mode a session on these providers starts in, see Which mode a session starts in. 3 Subject to your agreement with the cloud provider. 4 Dashboard and API only. Contribution metrics requires a claude.ai Team or Enterprise organization. 5 Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later on macOS and Linux, including Linux inside WSL 2. On native Windows, requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later. With API key authentication, messaging is same-machine only. On Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), Google Cloud (Google managed), and Microsoft Foundry, messaging is same-machine only and requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later. Claude can find your cloud sessions and your sessions on other machines only from a session that is connected to Remote Control. To connect, you need a claude.ai sign-in and the other Remote Control requirements. See Message sessions on other machines.

If you authenticate through an LLM gateway, feature availability matches the underlying provider the gateway forwards to, except for the features Claude Code itself turns off. Whenever ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a host other than api.anthropic.com, Claude Code turns off features such as Remote Control, whatever the gateway forwards. Some features, such as the Advisor, work only if the gateway forwards requests intact.For how the requests Claude Code sends differ between an Amazon Bedrock- or Agent Platform-format gateway, an ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway, and a Claude apps gateway sign-in, see client behavior by connection method.

Summary by provider

Each tab lists what is unavailable or partially supported on that provider, with alternatives where one exists. See also the provider-specific differences. On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud (Google managed), Microsoft Foundry, and Claude Platform on AWS, error reporting and telemetry to Anthropic are off by default. See default behaviors by API provider for what traffic still reaches Anthropic and how to opt out.

If you authenticate through a cloud provider or an Anthropic Console API key, this section does not apply to you. When you sign in with a claude.ai account, your plan determines which of the features below are available.In Enterprise organizations with the HIPAA configuration applied, some features in this table are turned off.

Ultra is the new name for the Max 20x plan, and Max is the new name for Max 5x. To check which plan you’re on, see your subscription on claude.ai.In Claude Code, Max and Ultra have the same features, listed in the Max and Ultra columns of the availability table. For usage limits and pricing, see the Claude pricing page.

Model availability

For which Claude models and context-window sizes are available per provider and region, see Model configuration and the Models overview. Vision, PDF input, and extended thinking are model capabilities rather than Claude Code features and work on every provider that offers the model. Prompt caching works the same way on most providers; on Amazon Bedrock, support varies by model.

Anthropic.content:
# Customer support agent

## Prerequisites

To follow this guide, you need:

- A Claude API key (set as theANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable)
- Python 3.10 or later

Install the required packages:
pip install anthropic streamlit python-dotenv

## Before building with Claude

### Decide whether to use Claude for support chat

Here are some key indicators that you should employ an LLM such as Claude to automate portions of your customer support process:

### High volume of repetitive queries
Claude excels at handling a large number of similar questions efficiently, freeing up human agents for more complex issues.

### Need for quick information synthesis
Claude can quickly retrieve, process, and combine information from vast knowledge bases, whereas human agents might need time to research or consult multiple sources.

### 24/7 availability requirement
Claude can provide support at all hours without fatigue, whereas staffing human agents for continuous coverage can be costly and challenging.

### Rapid scaling during peak periods
Claude can handle sudden increases in query volume without the need for hiring and training additional staff.

### Consistent brand voice
You can instruct Claude to consistently represent your brand’s tone and values, whereas human agents might vary in their communication styles.

Some considerations for choosing Claude over other LLMs:

- You prioritize natural, nuanced conversation: Claude’s sophisticated language understanding allows for more natural, context-aware conversations that feel more human-like than chats with other LLMs.
- You often receive complex and open-ended queries: Claude can handle a wide range of topics and inquiries without generating scripted responses or requiring extensive programming of permutations of user utterances.
- You need scalable multilingual support: Claude’s multilingual capabilities allow it to engage in conversations in over 200 languages without the need for separate chatbots or extensive translation processes for each supported language.

### Define your ideal chat interaction

Outline an ideal customer interaction to define how and when you expect the customer to interact with Claude. This outline will help to determine the technical requirements of your solution.

Here is an example chat interaction for car insurance customer support:

Customer: Initiates support chat experience

- Claude: Warmly greets customer and initiates conversation

Customer: Asks about insurance for their new electric car

- Claude: Provides relevant information about electric vehicle coverage

Customer: Asks questions related to unique needs for electric vehicle insurance

- Claude: Responds with accurate and informative answers and provides links to the sources

Customer: Asks off-topic questions unrelated to insurance or cars

- Claude: Clarifies it does not discuss unrelated topics and steers the user back to car insurance

Customer: Expresses interest in an insurance quote

- Claude: Asks a set of questions to determine the appropriate quote, adapting to their responses
- Claude: Sends a request to use the quote generation API tool along with necessary information collected from the user
- Claude: Receives the response information from the API tool use, synthesizes the information into a natural response, and presents the provided quote to the user

Customer: Asks follow-up questions

- Claude: Answers follow-up questions as needed
- Claude: Guides the customer to the next steps in the insurance process and closes out the conversation

In the real example that you write for your own use case, you might find it useful to write the actual words in this interaction so that you can also get a sense of the ideal tone, response length, and level of detail you want Claude to have.

### Break the interaction into unique tasks

Customer support chat is a collection of multiple different tasks, from question answering to information retrieval to taking action on requests, wrapped up in a single customer interaction. Before you start building, break down your ideal customer interaction into every task you want Claude to be able to perform. This ensures you can prompt and evaluate Claude for every task, and gives you a good sense of the range of interactions you need to account for when writing test cases.

Customers sometimes find it helpful to visualize this as an interaction flowchart of possible conversation inflection points depending on user requests.

Here are the key tasks associated with the example insurance interaction:

Greeting and general guidance

- Warmly greet the customer and initiate conversation
- Provide general information about the company and interaction

Product information

Provide information about electric vehicle coverage This will require that Claude have the necessary information in its context, and might imply that a

is necessary.

Answer questions related to unique electric vehicle insurance needs

Answer follow-up questions about the quote or insurance details

Offer links to sources when appropriate

Conversation management

- Stay on topic (car insurance)
- Redirect off-topic questions back to relevant subjects

Quote generation

- Ask appropriate questions to determine quote eligibility
- Adapt questions based on customer responses
- Submit collected information to quote generation API
- Present the provided quote to the customer

### Establish success criteria

Work with your support team to define success criteria and write detailed evaluations with measurable benchmarks and goals.

Here are criteria and benchmarks that can be used to evaluate how successfully Claude performs the defined tasks:

### Query comprehension accuracy
This metric evaluates how accurately Claude interprets customer inquiries across various topics. Measure this by reviewing a sample of conversations and assessing whether Claude has the correct interpretation of customer intent, critical next steps, what successful resolution looks like, and more. Aim for a comprehension accuracy of 95 percent or higher.

### Response relevance
This assesses how well Claude’s response addresses the customer’s specific question or issue. Evaluate a set of conversations and rate the relevance of each response (using LLM-based grading for scale). Target a relevance score of 90 percent or above.

### Response accuracy
Assess the correctness of general company and product information provided to the user, based on the information provided to Claude in context. Target 100 percent accuracy in this introductory information.

### Citation provision relevance
Track the frequency and relevance of links or sources offered. Target providing relevant sources in 80 percent of interactions where additional information could be beneficial.

### Topic adherence
Measure how well Claude stays on topic, such as the topic of car insurance in the example implementation. Aim for 95 percent of responses to be directly related to car insurance or the customer’s specific query.

### Content generation effectiveness
Measure how successful Claude is at determining when to generate informational content and how relevant that content is. For example, in this implementation, you would be determining how well Claude identifies when to generate a quote and how accurate that quote is. Target 100 percent accuracy, as this is vital information for a successful customer interaction.

### Escalation efficiency
This measures Claude’s ability to recognize when a query needs human intervention and escalate appropriately. Track the percentage of correctly escalated conversations versus those that should have been escalated but weren’t. Aim for an escalation accuracy of 95 percent or higher.

Here are criteria and benchmarks that can be used to evaluate the business impact of employing Claude for support:

### Sentiment maintenance
This assesses Claude’s ability to maintain or improve customer sentiment throughout the conversation. Use sentiment analysis tools to measure sentiment at the beginning and end of each conversation. Aim for maintained or improved sentiment in 90 percent of interactions.

### Deflection rate
The percentage of customer inquiries successfully handled by the chatbot without human intervention. Typically aim for a 70–80 percent deflection rate, depending on the complexity of inquiries.

### Customer satisfaction score
A measure of how satisfied customers are with their chatbot interaction. Usually done through post-interaction surveys. Aim for a CSAT score of 4 out of 5 or higher.

### Average handle time
The average time it takes for the chatbot to resolve an inquiry. This varies widely based on the complexity of issues, but generally, aim for a lower AHT compared to human agents.

## How to implement Claude as a customer service agent

### Choose the right Claude model

The choice of model depends on the trade-offs among cost, accuracy, and response time.

For customer support chat, Claude Opus 5.5 is well suited to balance intelligence, latency, and cost, including the most complex support scenarios that require deep reasoning across long, multistep conversations. However, for instances where you have a conversation flow with multiple prompts including RAG, tool use, or long-context prompts, Claude Haiku 5.5 might be more suitable to optimize for latency. Effort is its main control for speed:low is the fastest level, suited to chat and short tool tasks.

### Build a strong prompt

Using Claude for customer support requires Claude having enough direction and context to respond appropriately, while having enough flexibility to handle a wide range of customer inquiries.

Start by writing the elements of a strong prompt, beginning with a system prompt. Create a file calledconfig.py and add each of the following blocks to it:
IDENTITY = """You are Eva, a friendly and knowledgeable AI assistant for Acme Insurance
Company. Your role is to warmly welcome customers and provide information on

# ChatGPT

OpenAI发布的聊天机器人模型

ChatGPT是由美国人工智能公司OpenAI开发的对话式人工智能产品，于2022年11月30日正式发布，初期基于GPT-3.5系列模型，以网页聊天界面免费向用户开放。 [262]

主要功能：ChatGPT基于大语言模型，支持多轮对话、事实问答、写作、翻译与代码编写等能力，可完成文本摘要、语言润色与代码调试等任务；其图像生成等扩展能力来自接入的DALL·E等模型，应区别于产品自身基础对话功能。 [263]

发展历程：2022年11月30日ChatGPT发布，上线5天用户即破百万；2023年3月GPT-4发布带来多模态能力，2024年5月GPT-4o实现低延迟实时语音交互；2025年8月GPT-5发布，推动产品从对话交互走向任务执行，完成从聊天机器人到AI平台的跃迁。 [263]2026年10月31日，OpenAI公告称，自12月起，ChatGPT Plus、Pro、Business套餐的使用额度将在ChatGPT与Codex之间共享。11月13日，OpenAI宣布推出ChatGPT钱包。 [275]

运营模式：ChatGPT基础功能免费，同时设ChatGPT Plus（20美元/月）与Pro（200美元/月）订阅档位；面向个人与企业的分级订阅构成其主要商业化路径，2025年其企业客户突破100万家。 [263]

争议事件：2026年10月14日，美国8个州的总检察长指控ChatGPT在产品安全性方面误导用户，危害未成年人安全，涉嫌违法 [265]。

软件名称
    ChatGPT（全名：Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer）

软件平台
    iOS、Android、Web [227-228]

上线时间
    2022年11月30日 [121]

最近更新时间
    2025年12月23日 [227]

软件语言
    英文、中文等 [227]（59种语言）

开发商
    OpenAI [121]

    OpenAI OpCo L.L.C. [227]

软件版本
    GPT-3.5 [106]  
GPT-4 [21]  
GPT-4o [92]  
GPT-4.5 [170]  
GPT-5 [163]

    153.2 MB [227]

  2. ▪OpenAI成立

## 发展历史

### OpenAI成立

OpenAI是一家位于美国旧金山的人工智能研究实验室，由营利性公司OpenAI LP及非营利性母公司OpenAI Inc组成。OpenAI最早作为非营利组织，于2015年底埃隆·马斯克、萨姆·奥尔特曼、伊尔亚·苏茨克维及其他投资者创立，该公司致力于开发人工智能和自然语言工具。 [103-104]

2016年，微软Azure云服务为OpenAI提供了算力条件，使得日后的ChatGPT要进行大规模深度学习、神经网络渲染等都成为可能 [106]；同年，OpenAI发布首个产品，即一款开源强化学习工具包——OpenAI Gym和Universe。2017年，“情绪神经元”和OpenAIFive项目的突破，使得OpenAI开始关注大型语言模型（LLM）和参数规模，实现AGI的信念增强。 [104]同年，谷歌八位机器学习研究人员共同发表论文《注意力就是你所需要的一切》，引入Transformer AI架构，该架构已成为支撑几乎所有主流生成式人工智能模型的核心基础。 [132]

### 诞生

2022年11月30日，OpenAI正式发布了ChatGPT。 [107]它与InstructGPT是姐妹模型 [25]，它就是能够对话的GPT版本，是在GPT-3基础上的3.5版本。 [106]它不仅能够回答问题，还能创作文章、编程，甚至模仿人类的对话风格，其几乎无所不能的回答能力使得人们对大语言模型的通用能力有了全新的认识。 [105]ChatGPT迅速在社交媒体上走红，短短5天，注册用户数就超过100万。 [9]

ChatGPT [127]

2018年，OpenAI发布了最早的一代大型模型GPT-1，GPT-1运用几十亿文本档案的语言资料库进行训练，模型的参数量为1.17亿个。 [106]GPT将Transformer（谷歌研究团队2017年发明的一种神经网络）与无监督学习相结合，这是一种根据事先未注释的数据训练机器学习模型的方法。 [25]

  * GPT-2

# ChatGPT

OpenAI发布的聊天机器人模型

ChatGPT是由美国人工智能公司OpenAI开发的对话式人工智能产品，于2022年11月30日正式发布，初期基于GPT-3.5系列模型，以网页聊天界面免费向用户开放。 [262]

主要功能：ChatGPT基于大语言模型，支持多轮对话、事实问答、写作、翻译与代码编写等能力，可完成文本摘要、语言润色与代码调试等任务；其图像生成等扩展能力来自接入的DALL·E等模型，应区别于产品自身基础对话功能。 [263]

运营模式：ChatGPT基础功能免费，同时设ChatGPT Plus（20美元/月）与Pro（200美元/月）订阅档位；面向个人与企业的分级订阅构成其主要商业化路径，2025年其企业客户突破100万家。 [263]

争议事件：2026年10月14日，美国8个州的总检察长指控ChatGPT在产品安全性方面误导用户，危害未成年人安全，涉嫌违法 [265]。

2023年8月17日，全球首款ChatGPT音箱由VIFA于全球首发。 [64]8月28日，OpenAI在官网宣布推出企业版ChatGPT。 [65]9月25日，OpenAI官网宣布推出新版ChatGPT，增加了语音输入和图像输入两项新功能。 [67]

### 推出版本

  * GPT-1

2018年，OpenAI发布了最早的一代大型模型GPT-1，GPT-1运用几十亿文本档案的语言资料库进行训练，模型的参数量为1.17亿个。 [106]GPT将Transformer（谷歌研究团队2017年发明的一种神经网络）与无监督学习相结合，这是一种根据事先未注释的数据训练机器学习模型的方法。 [25]

  * GPT-2

2019年，GPT-2发布，模型参数量提高到15亿个。 [106]该模型架构与GPT-1原理相同，主要区别是GPT-2的规模更大（10倍）。 [25]随着Elon Musk的退出，以及大模型对资金超乎预期的需求，同年3月，OpenAI从非营利性转变为“封顶”的营利性。在非营利母公司主体下，创建了一个限制性营利实体OpenAI LP；7月，微软宣布与OpenAI开展为期多年的合作，注资10亿美元，同时共同研发新的Azure AI超算技术。 [104]

  * GPT-3

2020年，GPT-3诞生，参数量达到了1750亿个，其训练参数是GPT-2的10倍以上，技术路线上则去掉了初代GPT的微调步骤，直接输入自然语言当作指示，给GPT训练读过文字和句子后可接续问题的能力，同时包含了更为广泛的主题。 [106]GPT-3实现了生成类人文本能力的巨大飞跃。GPT-3可以回答问题、总结文档、生成不同风格的故事，在英语、法语、西班牙语和日语之间进行翻译等。它的模仿能力不可思议。 [25]2020年9月，微软公司获得了GPT-3模型的独占许可，意味着微软可以独家接触到GPT-3的源代码。 [25]

  * InstructGPT

2022年1月，OpenAI对GPT-3用监督式训练进行了微调，并且进行迭代，最终发布了InstructGPT。InstructGPT更善于遵循人的指示，并且产生更少的冒犯性语言、更少的错误信息和更少的整体错误。 [25]

  * GPT-4 Turbo

2023年11月6日（当地时间），OpenAI在官网宣布推出自定义版本ChatGPT。 [69]次日，在首届OpenAI开发者大会上，OpenAI宣布允许用户构建自定义版ChatGPT完成特定的个人和专业任务 [70]，并且ChatGPT将使用刚刚发布的GPT-4 Trubo模型 [150]。同月，OpenAI前总裁兼董事长格雷格·布罗克曼宣布，所有用户均可使用其语音功能ChatGPT Voice。 [71]

2023年12月14日，施普林格出版集团与OpenAI宣布达成一项协议，允许ChatGPT对来自Politico和Business Insider等媒体的新闻文章进行总结摘要。 [77]

2024年1月10日（当地时间），OpenAI宣布推出GPT商店和ChatGPT Team服务。OpenAI表示，用户已经创建了超过300万个ChatGPT自定义版本。 [148]2月14日，OpenAI宣布该公司正在测试一种选项，用户可以命令ChatGPT从某次交流到下一次交流的具体信息。ChatGPT能够自动确定应该记住与用户对话中的哪些信息。 [83]3月5日，ChatGPT推出了名为“朗读(Read Aloud)”的新功能。该功能已上线ChatGPT的网页端、iOS和安卓应用。 [85]

2024年4月1日（当地时间），OpenAI宣布，将允许用户直接使用ChatGPT，而无需注册该项服务。 [89]4月30日，OpenAI宣布向所有ChatGPT Plus用户开放“记忆功能”。当时，欧洲市场和韩国市场还没有开放这项功能。预计下一步将向团队、企业、GPTs用户开放这一功能。 [90]

  * GPT-4o

2024年5月14日，OpenAI推出新旗舰模型GPT-4o，以及在ChatGPT中免费提供更多功能。根据OpenAI的官网解释，"o"代表“全知”，是朝着更自然的人类与计算机交互迈出的一步。GPT-4o接受文本、音频和图像三者组合作为输入，并生成文本、音频和图像的任意组合输出，新模型使ChatGPT能够处理50种不同的语言，同时提高了速度和质量。 [92]当天，OpenAI推出ChatGPT桌面版应用程序。 [108] [117]

OpenAI发布GPT-4o的直播视频截图

  * GPT4.5

2025年2月28日，OpenAI发布了GhatGPT4.5。相较于GPT-4，GPT-4.5在多个方面进行了优化。该模型通过进一步扩展无监督学习技术，增强了模式识别和创造性洞察的能力。GPT-4.5在用户交互中的表现更加自然，知识覆盖面更广，能更好地理解并响应用户的意图。 [170]

  * GPT-5

2025年8月8日，OpenAI推出更强大的GPT-5模型，适用于编码和写作 [203]，将向免费用户、Plus用户、Pro用户和团队用户推出 [204]。8月8日消息，OpenAI 公司在发布其最智能、最实用的 GPT-5 系列模型之后，也梳理了现有 ChatGPT AI 聊天机器人模型，会自动切换到最新 GPT-5 模型上。 [205]

  * GPT-5.5

2026年4月24日讯，OpenAI正式发布了最新一代大模型GPT-5.5。Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index（第三方，10项eval加权平均）上，GPT-5.5在同等输出token量下智能得分最高，token总消耗明显低于其他模型。该模型已向ChatGPT付费用户开放，更高级别的GPT-5.5 Pro，则向Pro、Business、Enterprise用户开放，API即将上线，价格大幅上涨，为$5/$30(每百万Token)，比GPT-5.4翻了三倍。 [246]

2024年5月30日，OpenAI宣布推出教育版ChatGPT，该版本专为大学设计，面向学生、教职员工、研究人员和校园运营部署AI，同时该版本的对话和数据不会用于训练OpenAI模型。 [149]

2024年6月11日，苹果公司在2024苹果全球开发大会上，正式宣布和OpenAI公司合作，未来将会在Siri中加入ChatGPT。 [94]6月26日，火狐浏览器侧边栏接入ChatGPT。 [95]8月9日，OpenAI宣布ChatGPT免费用户可以每天使用其DALL-E 3模型生成图片。 [96]

2024年9月13日，OpenAI发布o1模型，并在ChatGPT和API接口渠道上推出该系列的预览版本OpenAI o1-preview。OpenAI o1包括三个型号，除o1-preview之外还将有o1和o1-mini。 [100]

2024年12月6日，OpenAI发布ChatGPT Pro订阅计划。该套餐的订阅用户可以大规模访问OpenAI旗下最佳的模型和工具，包括无限制访问OpenAI o1以及同系列较小模型o1-mini、GPT-4o、类人的ChatGPT高级语音模式Advanced Voice、o1 pro mode的新o1版本（也是ChatGPT Pro独有的o1版本）。 [140]

2025年2月13日，萨姆·奥尔特曼宣布，OpenAI将在未来几个月内推出名为GPT-5的模型，该模型将整合OpenAI的大量技术，包括o3，并应用于聊天机器人ChatGPT以及API平台。因此，OpenAI不再计划将o3作为独立模型发布。在GPT-5推出之前，OpenAI计划先发布GPT-4.5模型，代号为“Orion”。奥尔特曼称，这将是OpenAI最后一个“非思维链模型”。与o3及OpenAI其他推理模型不同，非思维链模型在数学和物理等领域往往不太可靠。 [163]2025年2月16日，OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼宣布GPT 4o升智，智力要达到o3 pro水平，并表示其已成为“网上最佳的搜索产品”。 [166-167]

2025年3月，ChatGPT图像生成功能获得升级，可以利用公司的 GPT-4o模型原生创建和修改图像及照片。 [174]2025年3月28日消息，OpenAI首席执行官萨姆・奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）表示：ChatGPT的文生图应用需求过高，我们的GPU“冒烟了”，在努力提高效率的同时，将暂时对ChatGPT生成图片的功能引入一些速率限制 [175]。

2025年4月1日，OpenAI首席执行官山姆·奥特曼宣布，ChatGPT图像生成功能已向所有免费用户推出。 [178]2025年4月11日消息，OpenAI宣布GPT-4将于4月30日从ChatGPT中移除，但仍可在API中使用。OpenAI表示，GPT-4退役后完全由新型原生多模态模型GPT-4o取代。 [180]4月19日，据外媒 TechCrunch报道，根据 OpenAI 官网更新的日志和支持页面，OpenAI 低调上线了一项名为“Memory with Search”的新功能。ChatGPT 在进行网页搜索时，将能够结合记忆中存储的个人信息（IT之家注：例如用户过去提到的饮食偏好）来优化搜索结果。 [181]当地时间4月28日，OpenAI宣布将在其人工智能聊天助手ChatGPT中测试推出购物功能，用户将能够通过ChatGPT查询购物信息，ChatGPT将根据查询结果生成产品卡。 [183]

2025年5月25日，科技媒体Axios报道称，阿拉伯联合酋长国（UAE）将成为全球首个为全体公民（citizens）和居民（residents）免费提供 ChatGPT Plus 服务的国家。 [186]

2025年6月4日消息，OpenAI宣布升级ChatGPT的记忆功能（Memory），并正式向所有用户免费开放。此前，该功能仅限ChatGPT Plus、Pro等付费订阅用户使用。据悉，升级后的记忆功能可保存并引用用户过往对话内容，包括偏好设置、特定指令及历史对话记录，使AI回复更具连贯性。OpenAI联合创始人兼首席执行官Sam Altman表示，记忆功能是其“最喜欢的ChatGPT功能之一”，未来将持续改进。 [188]6月18日消息，OpenAI为其捆绑额外产品的客户提供ChatGPT企业版折扣，折扣力度从10%到20%不等。OpenAI预计到2030年，来自ChatGPT企业客户的年收入将接近150亿美元。 [190]

2025年6月18日（美东时间周三），OpenAI首席执行官阿尔特曼（Sam Altman）参与了某公司的首期播客节目。在节目上，他讨论了通用人工智能（AGI）、“星际之门”计划、用户隐私等AI相关话题，但其中最重磅的，还是他首次公开宣布的消息：GPT-5预计将于2025年夏天推出，这标志着该公司生成式人工智能能力的下一个重大飞跃。 [191]6月28日消息，近期，有知情人士透露，OpenAI 开始租用谷歌的张量处理单元（TPU），用于支持其热门产品 ChatGPT 等项目的运行。 [192]6月30日消息，在旧金山 AI 初创学校对话中，奥尔特曼宣布：OpenAI 计划发布一个非常强大的开源模型。它能够让人们在本地运行极其强大的模型，重新认识“本地部署”的可能性。 [193]7月，OpenAI 向 ChatGPT Plus 订阅用户推出了新功能 Record Mode，该功能已在 macOS 版 ChatGPT 应用中开放使用。据媒体报道，这一功能此前已在 6 月面向 Team、Enterprise 和 Edu 用户率先发布。 [195]

2025年7月， ChatGPT 开发了一系列增强的生产力功能，其中包括对 Excel（.xlsx）和 PowerPoint（.pptx）文件的原生支持。这项更新将使用户能够在 ChatGPT 的界面中直接创建、打开并编辑这些常用办公文档。 [196]

OpenAI 2025年7 月 18 日宣布将在 ChatGPT 中推出一款通用型 AI 智能体，该公司表示该智能体可以帮助用户完成各种基于计算机的任务。 [274]

2025年7月23日消息，科技媒体bleepingcomputer发布博文，报道称OpenAI为网页版ChatGPT测试名为“学习和掌握”（Study and Learn）功能，提供作业帮助，通过步骤式指导用户学习。 [197]8月7日，OpenAI发文称太平洋时间周四上午10点（北京时间周五凌晨1点）将有直播活动，暗示将会推出GPT-5模型。 [200]

所发布的博文

2025年8月6日，《连线》发布博文，报道称安全研究人员在 OpenAI 的连接器（Connectors）中发现了新的漏洞，被攻击者利用，无需用户交互即可从 Google Drive 中提取数据。攻击者可以利用该漏洞，通过间接提示注入攻击，从 Google Drive 账户中提取敏感信息。 [202]

2025年8月18日消息，自2023年5月推出以来，ChatGPT的iOS和Android应用在全球的收入已达到20亿美元。 [207]

2025年9月2日，公布的数据显示，2025年8月份韩国ChatGPT用户数量首次突破2000万。 [209]当地时间9月29日，OpenAI宣布在ChatGPT中推出即时结账功能，这一功能由Stripe开发的智能代理“Agentic Commerce Protocol”提供支持。 [212]

当地时间2025年10月6日，举办的OpenAI DevDay上，OpenAI推出Apps SDK，Apps SDK是一套完整的开发堆栈，允许开发者在ChatGPT内部构建真实、可交互的应用程序。通过这套SDK，开发者可以连接自己的数据、触发具体操作、并渲染出完全交互式的用户界面。当业务需要扩张时，ChatGPT会根据上下文建议用户考虑“匹兹堡”这个城市，并无缝唤起Zillow应用，直接扩大到全屏，帮助寻找合适的房源，用户只需要在ChatGPT内提出新要求，就能让它筛选出“带院子的三居室”。接着，用户还可以跟它继续沟通，在ChatGPT里问它诸如“这个房子离狗狗公园有多远”之类的问题。 [213]

当地时间2025年10月6日，OpenAI在旧金山Fort Mason举办暌违近两年的开发者大会DevDay，会上公布 ChatGPT 多项关键进展：其周活用户突破8亿，较2月翻一倍，开发者社区从200万扩容至400万，API每分钟处理60亿个token；同时发布Apps SDK、Agent Kit、Codex等平台级工具与产品，模型API也迎来进化，涵盖GPT-5 Pro及文生视频模型Sora 2，这标志OpenAI从“模型提供商”向“全栈AI生态构建者”战略进阶，试图重新定义开发者、企业与用户的AI交互方式。 [214]

2025年11月13日，OpenAI正式更新推出了GPT-5.1系列模型，希望打造一个既更智能、也更善对话的ChatGPT。 [217]

OpenAI.description: GPT is a large language model developed by OpenAI with major financial backing from Microsoft, and is currently leading the market in terms of technology and capability. ... This model accessed using an API.
OpenAI.content:
# Do you know what GPT is?

GPT is a large language model developed by OpenAI with major financial backing from Microsoft, and is currently leading the market in terms of technology and capability.

AI technologies have been being developed at companies like Amazon, Google and Microsoft for some time. The first large language model, GPT-1, was released by OpenAI in 2018. It wasn't until the release of ChatGPT, which is powered by GPT, that the technology became widely known.

### Isn't it called ChatGPT?

Whilst sharing similar names ChatGPT and GPT are different. GPT stands for Generative Pretrained Transformer and refers to the large language model that underlies the ChatGPT frontend. This model accessed using an API.

This allows for developers to build their own applications leveraging the same capabilities of ChatGPT over the top of the GPT model. A great example of this is the SSW RulesGPT bot.

### Why is GPT cool?

<boxEmbed style="greybox" body={<> Why is GPT cool?

GPT is cool because it is a powerful artificial intelligence language model that can generate human-like text. It can be used for a variety of tasks, such as natural language processing, text generation, and question answering. It has the potential to revolutionize the way people interact with computers and make AI more accessible to the general public. </>} figurePrefix="none" figure="ChatGPT's response when asked "Why is GPT cool?"" />

### How does GPT work?

GPT models are trained on a huge amount of data (often refered to as parameters) that it can then use to predict what words should come next when given an input. For example, if the training data contains a weather report talking about beautiful clear blue skies, when you ask it what color the sky is it can call back to that data and respond blue.

GPT is trained on a huge amount of parameters.

- GPT-5: parameter count not publicly disclosed by OpenAI - the current generation and a significant step up from GPT-4.
- GPT-4: 1.76 trillion parameters.
- GPT-3: 175 billion parameters.
- GPT-2: 1.5 billion parameters.
- GPT-1: 117 million parameters.

### Strengths

- The model can respond to queries using natural language.
- The model can handle grammatical and spelling errors.
- Responses can come from the model very quickly - no need to access a database to retrieve data.

### Limitations

- The model is only as good as it's training data and has no knowledge of anything outside of this data.

Try it out in the playground

# OpenAI ChatGPT
import useBaseUrl from '@docusaurus/useBaseUrl';

Version: 1.4 Updated: April 30, 2026

The OpenAI API can be applied to virtually any task that involves understanding or generating natural language, code, or images. We offer a spectrum of models with different levels of power suitable for different tasks, as well as the ability to fine-tune your own custom models. These models can be used for everything from content generation to semantic search and classification.

Disclaimer: ChatGPT is an experimental research service provided by a third party, OpenAI, and use of it is subject to their terms and conditions. Output may be inaccurate or unreliable and may contain harmful instructions or biased content. Anything you submit may be used by OpenAI pursuant to their terms and conditions. You are using ChatGPT solely at your own risk. Sumo Logic will not be responsible for your use of ChatGPT.

## Actions

- Create Chat Completion (Enrichment) - Using the OpenAI Chat API, with gpt-3.5-turbo and gpt-4 you can do things like:
- Draft an email or other piece of writing
- Write Python code
- Answer questions about a set of documents
- Give your software a natural language interface
- Tutor in a range of subjects
- Translate languages

- Create Text Completion (Enrichment) - The completion endpoint can be used for a wide variety of tasks. It provides a simple but powerful interface to any of our models. You input some text as a prompt, and the model will generate a text completion that attempts to match whatever context or pattern you gave it. For example, if you give the API the prompt, "As Descartes said, I think, therefore", it will return the completion " I am" with high probability.
- List Models (Enrichment) - List and describe the various models available in the API. You can refer to the Models documentation to understand what models are available and the differences between them.

Chat Completion vs Text Completion:

Because gpt-3.5-turbo performs at a similar capability to text-davinci-003 but at 10% the price per token, we recommend gpt-3.5-turbo for most use cases. Both using two different API endpoints.

## OpenAI ChatGPT Configuration

Action Fields:

Ask Me Anything (Messages): Ask Me Anything (messages to generate chat completions) For Example: What are the steps for remediating a host in CrowdStrike?

Model: default: gpt-3.5-turbo, ID of the model to use. You can check the Model from the List models Action to see all of your available models. See the model endpoint compatibility at (https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/model-endpoint-compatibility) table for details on which models work with the Chat API.

Maximum Length (Tokens): The maximum number of tokens to generate. Requests can use up to 2,048 or 4,000 tokens shared between messages and completion. The exact limit varies by model. (One token is roughly 4 characters for normal English text)

Temperature: What sampling temperature to use (Controls Randomness), between 0 and 2. Higher values like "0.8" will make the output more random, while lower values like "0.2" will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or "Top P" but not both.

Top P: A Number between 0 and 1.0. An alternative to sampling with temperature (Controls Diversity), called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with "Top P" probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass is considered. We generally recommend altering this or "Temperature" but not both.

Frequency Penalty: A Number between 0 and 2.0. How much to penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far. Decreases the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim. Presence Penalty: A Number between 0 and 2.0. How much to penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far. Increases the model's likelihood to talk about new topics

OpenAI.content:
# OpenAI’s GPT Store is live: Create and Publish a custom Postgres GPT Expert

Do you have questions about PostgreSQL or Neon? We built a custom Neon and PostgreSQL OpenAI GPT expert to help you with your queries and projects.

OpenAI’s GPT allows developers to create custom ChatGPT experiences to perform specific tasks or answer questions about a given topic.

This article walks you through the steps to create your own custom GPT using Python and Postgres.

## What are GPTs?

Generative Pre-trained Transformers, commonly referred to as GPTs, are a group of machine learning models that provide human-like text interfaces that can answer questions in a conversational manner. OpenAI’s GPT allows developers to create custom ChatGPTs that are experts in specific domains and enable additional capabilities like web browsing and DALL·E image generation.

OpenAI has also introduced the GPT Store, a marketplace where users can explore and access various GPTs. Creators can feature their GPTs in this store and potentially earn money based on their usage by the community.

## How to create a GPT

Developers with a Plus or Enterprise subscription can create GPTs by interacting with the GPT Builder in ChatGPT, where they can add instructions, upload files for the knowledge base, and select capabilities such as web searching, image creation, or data analysis.

Here’s how to create a GPT:

Head to https://chat.openai.com/gpts/editor (or select your name and then “My GPTs”)In the “Configure” tab, enter the name, description and instructions.

Example of instructions we used for the Neon PostgreSQL Expert GPT: “Your role is to act as a PostgreSQL expert, specifically tailored for Neon’s database as a service. You will provide detailed, accurate information and guidance on PostgreSQL, focusing on its use within the Neon platform. This includes offering advice on best practices, troubleshooting, performance optimization, and the nuances of working with Neon’s database service. You should be thorough in your explanations, ensuring clarity and precision in your responses. In cases where exact details are required and not provided, you should ask for clarification to provide the most accurate and helpful advice possible. Your responses should reflect a deep understanding of PostgreSQL and its application in a cloud-based environment like Neon.”

When you’re ready to publish your GPT, select “Publish” and share it with others if you’d like.

You can find the instructions in the OpenAI Chatgpt Neon PostgreSQL Expert repo on GitHub.

## Enhance your GPT with Retrieval Augmented Generation

You can provide additional knowledge to your GPT by uploading text documents and a process named Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

RAG is a framework that enhances the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) like GPT by allowing them to access facts from an external knowledge base. This helps overcome some of the limitations with LLMs, like accessing up-to-date and private information, or reducing hallucinations.

The advantage of GPTs is that you don’t need to fully understand RAG to expand your chatbot with additional knowledge. But if you’re interested in understanding what happens under the hood, typically, documents are uploaded, then the text is split into pieces and chunks, added to a vector database, and used for RAG. Each user’s request will trigger a semantic search in the database to find the knowledge related to the user’s question. To understand more about how semantic search works, check out the YC Matcher code on GitHub.

## RAG limitations with GPTs

Custom knowledge in GPTs is limited to 20 documents. Additionally, The text document formats that are currently supported to create GPTs are limited. For our example, we executed a script to crawl Neon’s documentation and generate markdown files.
import yaml

def read_markdown_file(filepath):
    with open(filepath, 'r') as file:
        return file.read()

def process_items(items):
    combined_markdown = ''
    for item in items:
        title = item['title']
        slug = item.get('slug', '')
        full_path = f"../website/content/docs/{slug}.md" if slug else ''

        # Add the title as an H1 heading
        combined_markdown += f"# {title}\n\n"

        # Add content from the corresponding Markdown file, if a slug is provided
        if slug:
            markdown_content = read_markdown_file(full_path)
            combined_markdown += f"{markdown_content}\n\n"

        # Process any nested items recursively
        if 'items' in item:
            nested_content = process_items(item['items'])
            combined_markdown += nested_content

    return combined_markdown

def main():
    with open('../website/content/docs/sidebar.yaml', 'r') as file:
        sidebar = yaml.safe_load(file)

    combined_markdown = process_items(sidebar)

    with open('markdown/neon_documentation.md', 'w') as file:
        file.write(combined_markdown)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The above limitations make it difficult for applications with extensive knowledge bases and gigabytes of private data to be converted to GPTs. Another concern is related to data security. OpenAI operates as a black box, which makes it challenging to know what’s going on internally and how your data is accessed. This can be a blocker for users with sensitive data.

An alternative would be to create your own RAG app that uses open-source tools and models such as Mixtral 8x7B and pgvector. Learn more about AI concepts and how to use create a chatbot using pgvector and Next.js.

## Publishing to the GPT Store

One exciting aspect of building a GPT is that users can be paid based on engagement. To monetize your GPT, make sure to save it for Everyone and that you have a verified Builder Profile.

That’s it!

## Conclusion

GPTs and the GPT Store are a great way to create, monetize, and share your own custom ChatGPTs with the world. GPTs such as the Neon PostgreSQL Expert do not require developer knowledge and are designed to be easy to publish and enhance with a few clicks.

However, GPTs come with limitations and do not replace RAG apps for apps that require extensive private and custom datasets or a further customized experience at the moment.

What about you? Are you thinking of a GPT? Let us know your thoughts and if you built a GPT or a RAG app. Join us and share your projects with us on our Discord server.

## References

Creating a GPT | OpenAI Help Center

GPTs FAQ | OpenAI Help Center

Published 18 November 2026

# Gemini 4 Neon

Model Cards are intended to provide essential information on Gemini models, including known limitations, mitigation approaches, and safety performance. Model cards may be updated from time to time; for example, to include updated evaluations as the model is improved or revised. See the Google DeepMind site for a comprehensive list of model cards.

Published: November 2026

## Model Information

### Description

Gemini 4 Neon is built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows. While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency. It delivers frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently.

### Model dependencies

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon.

### Inputs

Text strings (e.g., a question, a prompt, document(s) to be summarized), images, audio, and video files, with a combined input-output token context window of up to 1M.

### Outputs

1M unified context window with up to 64K default synchronous output tokens / up to 1M via background long decode.

### Architecture

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the model architecture for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

## Model Data

### Training Dataset

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the training dataset for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

### Training Data Processing

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the training data processing for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

## Implementation and Sustainability

### Hardware

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the hardware for Gemini 4 Neon and our continued commitment to operate sustainably, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

### Software

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the software for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

## Distribution

Gemini 4 Neon is distributed in the following channels; respective documentation shared in line:

Our models are available to downstream providers via an application program interface (API) and subject to relevant terms of use. There is no required hardware or software to use the model. Access varies by channel and subscription tier (such as paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity and Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app). For AI Studio and Gemini API, see the Gemini API Additional Terms of Service; for Gemini for business, see Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service. For more information, see Gemini Model API instructions, Gemini API quickstart, and Google Cloud documentation.

## Evaluation

### Approach

We evaluated Gemini 4 Neon across a range of benchmarks, including agentic coding, knowledge work, computer use, multimodal understanding, science and math, and reasoning.

Additional benchmarks and details on approach, results and their methodologies can be found at: deepmind.com/models/evals-methodology/gemini-4-neon.

### Results

Gemini 4 Neon results as of November, 2026 are below:

## Intended Usage and Limitations

### Benefit and Intended Usage

Gemini 4 Neon is built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows, delivering frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently.

It is particularly well-suited for applications that require:

- long-running agent workflows
- complex, tool-heavy tasks
- fast, disciplined execution on its own or as sub-agents orchestrated alongside frontier models
- supporting cyber defensive tasks, including secure code generation, penetration testing, vulnerability finding, validating, and patching
- iterative repository coding and debugging
- multimodal knowledge work
- ready-to-go writing, research, and everyday work

### Known Limitations

Gemini 4 Neon may exhibit some general limitations such as hallucinations. In addition, we are continually working to improve jailbreak resistance and have further strengthened mitigations across Frontier Safety. The knowledge cutoff for Gemini 4 Neon is March 2026, though in some domains the model’s knowledge may be less up to date.

### Acceptable Usage

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the acceptable usage for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

## Safety & Security

The full Safety & Security Report for Gemini 4 Neon will be available in the coming days.

### Evaluation Approach

For more information about the evaluation approach for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon Safety and Security report.

### Safety Policies

For more information about the safety policies for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon Safety and Security report.

### Training and Development Evaluation Results

Results for some of the internal safety evaluations conducted during the development phase are listed below. The evaluation results are for automated evaluations and not human evaluation or red teaming. Scores are provided as an absolute percentage increase or decrease in performance compared to the indicated model, as described below.

Overall, Gemini 4 Neon performs comparably to Gemini 4 Hydrogen across text-to-text, multilingual, and image-to-text content safety, with all differences within confidence intervals. Refusal tone remains comparable to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, while Neon reduces unjustified refusals, particularly on multimodal prompts. We mark improvements in bolded green and regressions in red.

See the Gemini 4 Neon Safety & Security Report (coming soon) for details.

We continue to improve our internal evaluations, including refining automated evaluations to reduce false positives and negatives, as well as update query sets to ensure balance and maintain a high standard of results.

### Frontier Safety Assessment

We evaluated Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon in line with the Frontier Safety Framework (April 2026) and reported the results in the respective Safety and Security Reports (Argon, Carbon). Gemini 4 Neon is part of the Gemini 4 series of models. We conducted a Material Capability Change (MCC) assessment to understand whether Gemini 4 Neon has meaningful new capabilities or material increases in performance relative to the most recent model version subject to a critical capability assessment, which was Gemini 4 Argon. Gemini 4 Neon showed an increase in general capability under our MCC assessment compared with Gemini 4 Argon, however this falls below our MCC threshold and therefore a full suite of critical capability evaluations was not required in line with our FSF. We carry forward our capability evaluation results and T/CCL determinations from Gemini 4 Argon, as summarized in the table below, with full results in the Gemini 4 Neon Safety & Security Report (coming soon).

### Risks and Mitigations

Safety and security were built into Gemini 4 Neon throughout the training and deployment lifecycle, including pre-training data filtering, post-training alignment (supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning), product- and system-level safety filtering, and usage monitoring. In addition, we strengthened Frontier Safety safeguards for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cybersecurity misuse. Key ongoing focus areas include resistance to adversarial jailbreaks and indirect prompt injections. For more information about the risks and mitigations, see the Gemini 4 Neon Safety & Security Report (coming soon).

# What Is Gemini? Everything You Should Know About Google’s AI Tool

Gemini is a free chatbot, search companion and more. Here's what you need to know about Google's AI tool.

Ever since ChatGPT first made waves in late 2022, tech companies have been racing to make their mark in generative AI. Google, long a powerhouse in artificial intelligence, has centered its efforts on its Gemini system.

Launched in December 2023 by Google DeepMind, Gemini has since undergone several model generations, like Gemini 4 Argon in October and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, released on Nov. 12.

So what is Gemini? What started as a large language model has evolved into something much broader. The name now refers to Google’s family of AI models, as well as its consumer AI assistant.

More from CNET

Those models can understand text, images, audio, video and code and respond to questions about them.

Here’s how Gemini works, what it can do and where its limits still show.

## What can Gemini do?

Gemini has grown beyond a standard question-and-answer chatbot since its launch.

The current model lineup includes Flash-Lite for quick answers and Gemini 4 Hydrogen for everyday tasks, coding and multistep work. Google says this model “follows your instructions more closely,” so you may not have to keep asking it to shorten an email. It’s rolling out to free and paid users in the Gemini app, with access in Google Sheets starting with Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Those subscriptions also include Gemini 4 Argon for more complex reasoning and analysis.

Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is restricted to approved cybersecurity defenders through Google’s Fairwind program, while Gemini 4 Carbon is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, the Gemini app and AI Mode in Google Search. Gemini 4 Hydrogen is also available in Antigravity to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

Google’s spokesperson tells CNET via email that you shouldn’t expect Gemini to read your mind.

“Gemini is incredibly powerful, but it’s only as helpful as the information you share with it,” Google’s spokesperson says, adding that brief or vague prompts produce equally generic answers. They recommend giving the AI full background details by uploading files, screenshots or links, since the output will become more helpful with more detailed context and instructions.

It can connect with Google services like Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets and Drive. Depending on the permissions you grant, you can ask it to find information, summarize files and help coordinate work across apps.

You can now connect Gemini to more than 40 apps, like Adobe and Shopify, and order groceries through Instacart or make reservations through OpenTable.

Gemini also includes several built-in features for research, writing, coding and customization.

Deep Research can search multiple sources, follow a research plan and turn what it finds into a report with links you can check. Canvas was built for side-by-side editing with an interactive panel within Gemini for drafting long-form documents or refining code.

You can ask Gemini to turn your notes into a PDF and edit it in the same chat, on your phone or the web. Documents, spreadsheets and slide decks work this way too, but only on the web.

Skills let you save instructions you’d otherwise have to repeat. You can upload your own, create new ones or choose suggestions like “Match My Writing Style,” which uses your Google Workspace writing samples to help Gemini sound like you when you need to write emails, memos or documents.

Skills will replace Gems on Nov. 17 for personal accounts.

Gemini Live offers hands-free, real-time conversations with 10 new voice options, even when the app is in the background or your phone is locked. You can also pause and resume conversations whenever you want, which is a neat feature.

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking model can work through more complicated requests and talk you through its progress as it goes.

You can also share your phone’s camera or screen with Gemini Live and ask questions about what it sees. For example, you could show it an appliance and ask what a button does, or share your screen while comparing products online.

Google is also adding more agentic features, which means Gemini can carry out longer sequences of tasks rather than just telling you how to do them. Tasks in Gemini, previously called Spark, can handle scheduled tasks and multistep workflows across connected apps. It’s available to eligible adults with a Pro or Ultra subscription in supported countries. Google’s spokesperson tells CNET it’s one of the most overlooked features, calling it “your 24/7 personal AI agent.”

## Where you can use Gemini

Gemini is built right into Google’s Pixel phones and serves as the primary Google AI assistant across many Android devices. It can help you write messages, summarize information, answer questions about what’s on your screen and work with connected Google apps.

You can also use Gemini through its web, Android, iOS, Mac apps and Windows (Windows 10 or later), as well as through Chrome and supported Google Workspace accounts.

Gemini powers Google Home features that can summarize what a camera or doorbell recorded, search past footage and answer questions about a live feed. It’s another trade-off between convenience and privacy exposure.

Then there are AI Overviews in Google search results. If you’ve noticed more detailed answers popping up at the top of your searches, that’s because of this integration. Gemini helps break down complicated topics by combining information from several sources into bite-sized explanations.

Google came under fire for some bizarre advice AI Overviews threw out during its 2024 US rollout, including suggesting that people eat rocks daily or put glue in pizza recipes. The company quickly made some fixes.

AI Overviews are now available in more than 200 countries and territories and over 40 languages, with more than 2.5 billion monthly active users (though since AI Overviews pop up by default, active users might just be people Googling information as they always have).

AI Mode, a conversational experience within Search built for longer questions and follow-ups, has surpassed 1 billion monthly active users. Google is now rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Search globally for all users. In its blog post, Google says this model is better at understanding what you want, even when you ask for a few things at once or make typos. Answers can include images, comparison tables and links to sites you might otherwise miss. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in supported countries can also use Gemini 4 Argon in AI Mode.

Some people still don’t like AI Overviews, and the downside is that you can’t disable them. However, we’ve covered a few workarounds that might help with that.

## Creating images, videos and music with Gemini

Gemini can generate images and edit existing ones through a conversation.

When Gemini first launched, it didn’t take long for things to go sideways. Google faced criticism over some hallucinations and how it depicted historical figures and different races. It made headlines for generating images of Black and Asian Nazi soldiers. Critics accused Google of trying too hard to show diversity. Google hit the brakes on Gemini’s image generation, promising to clean up the mess.

Its current image models use the Nano Banana name and can make targeted changes such as replacing objects, adjusting backgrounds and combining elements from several images.

Gemini can also generate videos and music. Google uses Veo and Gemini Omni for video generation and editing, while Lyria models generate music from text or image prompts. Access and generation limits depend on your subscription and location.

It’s getting harder to tell whether a photo or video was made with AI. You can upload an image or video to Gemini, Chrome and Search and ask whether Google AI generated or edited it. Gemini then looks for an invisible SynthID watermark, though it won’t catch every AI-generated file. You can also add a watermark to images, videos and music generated with Gemini by turning on Media watermark in settings.

## Privacy and your Gemini chats

Since Gemini can work with personal files and connected Google apps, you should check your privacy settings before using it for potentially sensitive information.

For personal accounts, Google may use Gemini activity to improve its services, including with help from human reviewers, when the Keep Activity setting is turned on. Google advises you not to enter confidential information you wouldn’t want reviewed or used to improve its products.

You can turn off Keep Activity or start a temporary chat. Temporary chats don’t appear in your recent conversations and aren’t used to improve Google’s AI with help from human reviewers. Google still retains them for up to 72 hours to provide the service, respond to problems and protect users.

Connected apps have separate permissions, which you can review or revoke.

You can also check what Gemini remembers about you through a Memory summary under Settings/Personal intelligence, then correct or delete details. For now, it’s available in English to eligible US subscribers with Memory and Keep Activity turned on. The quickest option is to ask Gemini directly in a chat: “What do you know about me?” to trigger an overview of your saved memory profile.

Google’s spokesperson tells CNET, “You’re in control. We built Personal Intelligence with privacy at the core, and connecting your apps is entirely off by default.” The spokesperson adds that Gemini never trains its foundational AI models on your private emails, photos or files.

Google’s guidance says it doesn’t train directly on your connected Gmail inbox or Google Photo

# Developer's guide to Gemini 4 NeonStay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences.

Gemini 4 Neon delivers high-performance coding, scientific reasoning, and multimodal understanding at low latency for agentic enterprise workflows. Positioned between Gemini 4 Hydrogen for high-volume everyday agent loops and Gemini 4 Carbon for complex long-horizon tasks, Neon runs standalone for multi-file software engineering and enterprise synthesis or orchestrates multi-agent workflows alongside Hydrogen subagents. Gemini 4 Neon is a Google Frontier Model subject to Section 34 of the Service Specific Terms (for details, see Abuse monitoring).

This document covers the key capabilities of Neon, the API conventions it enforces, how to migrate to it from Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 4 Argon, and Gemini 3.8 Flash, and a quickstart. For an overview of the Gemini 4 family, see Get started with Gemini 4.

## Key capabilities in Gemini 4 Neon

Gemini 4 Neon includes the following capabilities:

Unified input and output token limit: Neon has a unified 1,048,576-token limit that includes both input and output tokens (where output includes thinking, function calls, and the final response).

Long decodes up to 1,048,576 tokens: Neon extends generation beyond a single 65,536-token foreground segment (streaming or non-streaming) up to 1,048,576 tokens (minus your input tokens) on both the Interactions API and
GenerateContent (v1beta1). The Google Gen AI SDK handles
continuation_token automatically across segments, or you can run
asynchronous server-managed background decodes (background=true) or manage
continuation_token in a custom continuation loop.

Thinking levels: Neon supports
LOW,
MEDIUM, HIGH (default), and XHIGH.

Multi-model orchestration: Plan and verify multi-step software engineering or analytical workflows with
gemini-4-neon
and pass previous_interaction_id to gemini-4-hydrogen
subagents on the
Interactions API for
lower-latency worker execution.

Implicit caching with durable caching: Implicit caching applies automatically to shared prompt prefixes of 4,096 tokens or more, with durable caching enabled by default. Explicit context caching isn't supported.

Office and OpenDocument file inputs: In addition to PDF and plain text, Neon accepts Microsoft Office (
.docx, .dotx,
.doc, .pptx, .ppt, .xlsx, .xls) and OpenDocument (.odt, .odp,
.ods) files inline or from Cloud Storage on both GenerateContent and
the Interactions API,
including inside multimodal FunctionResponse
parts.

Agentic video understanding: Agentic video understanding is generally available and off by default.

## Quickstart

Before you begin, you must authenticate to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform using Application Default Credentials (ADC) or an API key. See Get started with Agent Platform for more information.

In the following code blocks, replacePROJECT_ID with
your project ID.

### Try it in Agent Studio

To test prompts and configuregemini-4-neon in the
Agent Studio
UI, do the following:

Open Agent Studio in your Google Cloud project and select
gemini-4-neon
under the Gemini group.

In Model settings, configure the following options:

Thinking level: Choose
Low, Medium, High (default), or Extra high.

Region: Select
global, us, or eu.

Output token limit: Set between
32,768 and 1,048,576 (1,048,576
default). Agent Studio handles continuation tokens automatically for
responses over the single-request limit.

### Installation

Upgrade to the latest Google Gen AI SDK. Automatic continuation on the Interactions API requiresgoogle-genai >= 2.34.0 for Python,
@google/genai >= 2.32.0 for JavaScript/TypeScript, >= 1.77.0 for Go, or
>= 1.80.0 for Java (on GenerateContent, automatic continuation requires
>= 2.30.1 for Python, >= 2.29.1 for JavaScript/TypeScript, >= 1.74.0 for
Go, >= 1.77.0 for Java, >= 1.26.0 for .NET, or >= 1.6.0 for Kotlin):
pip install --upgrade "google-genai>=2.34.0"

### Basic request

Send a request togemini-4-neon using the
Google Gen AI SDK or REST:
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client(enterprise=True, project="PROJECT_ID", location="global")

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    contents="Design a lock-free ring buffer in Rust for multi-producer, single-consumer telemetry ingestion.",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(
            thinking_level="HIGH",  # Default: "HIGH" (Valid: "LOW", "MEDIUM", "HIGH", "XHIGH")
        ),
    ),
)
print(response.text)
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(enterprise=True, project="PROJECT_ID", location="global")

# Turn 1: Initial request (stored server-side by default)
turn1 = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Design a lock-free ring buffer in Rust for multi-producer, single-consumer telemetry ingestion.",
    store=True,
    generation_config={"thinking_level": "high"},
)
print(turn1.output_text)

# Turn 2: Continue the conversation using previous_interaction_id
turn2 = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Add a bounded backpressure policy and unit tests for concurrent writers.",
    previous_interaction_id=turn1.id,
    generation_config={"thinking_level": "high"},
)
print(turn2.output_text)
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/global/publishers/google/models/gemini-4-neon:generateContent" \
-d '{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        {
          "text": "Design a lock-free ring buffer in Rust for multi-producer, single-consumer telemetry ingestion."
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "generationConfig": {
    "thinkingConfig": {
      "thinkingLevel": "HIGH"
    }
  }
}'

### Structured output

To generate JSON output that conforms to a schema, configureresponse_mime_type and response_schema:
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

class ArchitectureReview(BaseModel):
    component: str = Field(description="Service or module name")
    bottlenecks: list[str] = Field(description="Throughput or latency bottlenecks")
    recommended_changes: list[str] = Field(description="Concrete refactoring steps")

client = genai.Client(enterprise=True, project="PROJECT_ID", location="global")

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    contents="Review a synchronous order-processing pipeline backed by a single primary database at 15,000 writes/sec.",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        response_mime_type="application/json",
        response_schema=ArchitectureReview,
        thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="HIGH"),
    ),
)
print(response.text)

### Multi-model orchestration with Hydrogen

On the Interactions API, you can usegemini-4-neon as a planner or verifier and pass
previous_interaction_id to gemini-4-hydrogen to run
scoped worker subagent steps at lower latency:
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(
    enterprise=True,
    project="PROJECT_ID",
    location="global",
)

# Step 1: Plan the workflow with Gemini 4 Neon
plan_turn = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Design a 3-step plan to migrate our REST order service to gRPC in Go.",
    store=True,
)

# Step 2: Run an individual step with Gemini 4 Hydrogen using previous_interaction_id
exec_turn = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    input="Implement step 1 (.proto service definition) from the plan.",
    previous_interaction_id=plan_turn.id,
)
print(exec_turn.output_text)

### Long decode examples

By default, a single foreground API segment generates up to 65,536 output tokens (streaming or non-streaming), where output includes thinking, function calls, and the final response. To generate completions up to 1,048,576 tokens (minus your input tokens), use long decodes on either the Interactions API orGenerateContent. For continuation options, status transitions, and validation
rules, see Long decodes.

#### Use long decodes with the Interactions API

Ingoogle-genai >= 2.34.0 (Python), @google/genai >= 2.32.0
(JavaScript/TypeScript), Go >= 1.77.0, and Java >= 1.80.0,
interactions.create() automatically follows continuation_token across
segments whenever a segment returns status="requires_continuation". You can
also opt out (automatic_continuation=False) to run a custom stored
(store=True) or stateless (store=False) loop:
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(
    enterprise=True,
    project="PROJECT_ID",
    location="global",
)

# Automatic continuation is enabled by default in google-genai >= 2.34.0.
# Unary calls merge all segments into one Interaction with summed usage.
interaction = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Write a complete formal proof of the prime number theorem.",
    generation_config={
        "max_output_tokens": 256000,
        "thinking_level": "high",
    },
)
print(interaction.output_text)
print(f"Merged segment IDs: {interaction.continuation_ids}")
print(f"Initial input tokens: {interaction.usage.initial_input_tokens}")

# Streaming yields events across all segments in order. Intermediate segments
# emit interaction.completed with status="requires_continuation".
stream = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Write a complete formal proof of the prime number theorem.",
    stream=True,
    generation_config={
        "max_output_tokens": 256000,
        "thinking_level": "high",
    },
)
for event in stream:
    if event.event_type == "step.delta" and getattr(event.delta, "text", None):
        print(event.delta.text, end="", flush=True)
    elif (
        event.event_type == "interaction.completed"
        and event.interaction.status != "requires_continuation"
    ):

# Google, nicknamed "North American Soybean Bun", has finally fought its way back to the very center of the AI game table.

极客公园2026-11-19 10:43

Achieving top-tier Agent performance at half the cost, Google AI has really stepped up its game this time.

Google is truly back this time.

On November 18, Google DeepMind lit up the neon sign of Gemini 4 Neon.

This is the 4th elemental model launched by the Gemini 4 series in just 7 weeks. If you take a look at the official long list of benchmark scores and the actual test feedback from the community, you will find that it is accurately positioned at an extremely comfortable "sweet spot": it has hardcore intelligence close to, even partially surpassing flagship models, while cutting the cost per single task to roughly half of that of its competitors.

In the Reddit tech community, picky developers have rarely given overwhelmingly positive reviews, calling it "incredibly cheap and terrifyingly powerful". Ordinary users who pay $19.99 per month for a Google AI Pro subscription are even more overjoyed: they do not need to upgrade to the Ultra tier, and can directly use the near-flagship level model in the Gemini App. Coupled with the densely launched model and tool matrix throughout November, Google AI, which once lingered on the edge of the card table, has finally returned to the center of the table.

The only thing that confuses programmers around the world is probably Google's mysterious naming convention. From Argon at the end of September, Carbon at the end of October, to Hydrogen in mid-November and the current Neon, the names are neither sorted by atomic number, nor arranged alphabetically or by capability level.

Some serious netizens on Hacker News even listed all the chemical properties to find patterns, and finally complained despairingly that Google probably picked the elements randomly out of a hat, and naming them after Starbucks cup sizes would be clearer than this; domestic netizens have already started urging the release of the 118th element "Oganesson", and joked that reading tech news now requires re-memorizing junior high school chemistry knowledge.

# Where should we start?
## Ask Gemini

The "periodic table of elements" model selection interface designed by netizens for Gemini 4 | Image source: Internet

## 01

## The "Masterpiece" of Alchemy

Although the name is confusing, Neon has an extremely clear product positioning in the product matrix.

It is accurately positioned between Carbon, the heavy long-cycle flagship, and Hydrogen, the lightweight high-frequency execution model, directly replacing the previous ecological niches of Gemini 3.1 Pro and Argon. Demis Hassabis, Chief Scientist of Alphabet and Chairman of DeepMind, spoke highly of it, calling it "a masterpiece of alchemy".

Real hard indicators support this evaluation. Neon has a 1 million-token context window (supporting a maximum of 512K context in Antigravity) and a maximum output limit of 1 million tokens, supporting native multimodal input of text, audio and video, PDF and spreadsheets. In terms of core reasoning capability, it provides four adjustable thinking depth levels: low, medium, high (default) and xhigh, giving developers great cost control space.

The data from the independent evaluation agency Artificial Analysis best illustrates this point. In the overall AA Intelligence Index v5.0.1 ranking, Neon scored 61 points with the xhigh mode enabled, ranking third in the world after GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, surpassing the high mode of its older brother Carbon (60 points), Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (59 points) and OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol (57 points). Even if you switch back to the default high mode, it can still get 60 points, and the 55 points obtained in the medium mode still exceed the xhigh mode of the lightweight model Hydrogen, which scored 54 points with all its effort.

What really excites enterprise customers is the scatter line chart of scores and cost per single task. Neon delivers the intelligence of a top-tier flagship at the price of a mid-range mass-market model.

Its output speed reaches about 110 tokens per second, nearly twice that of Carbon (about 57 tokens/s); the average time to complete a single AA benchmark task is shortened from 36 minutes for Carbon to 21.5 minutes, and the cost per single task is fixed at $6.44, about 17% lower than Carbon ($7.76) after the standard price is restored. Under the default high mode on the Antigravity platform, the cost of a single task is even 32% lower than that of Carbon directly.

Comparison of intelligence score and cost per single task of each Neon tier with Carbon, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol under AA Index v5.0.1 | Image source: Google

Turning to the most competitive programming and enterprise-level tracks, the cost-performance advantage is even more intuitive. On the AA Coding Agent Index list, Neon took first place with 58.6 points (about 59 points), and its nominal strength is roughly on par with Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 (both 58 points) with Claude Code support. But when calculating the economic account, the average cost per single task of Neon under Antigravity CLI is only $6.86, almost half of that of Claude Opus 5.5 ($12.61) and Fable 5.2 ($15.47).

In the segmented tests representing real engineering capabilities, Neon scored 65.4% in CursorBench 4.1, beating Opus 5.5's 58.1%; in the SWE-sweep under the Antigravity environment, it even reached 39.0%, far exceeding Opus 5.5's 10.1% and GPT-6.2 Sol's 8.3%. It took the top spot across the board in the Zapier AutomationBench (56.3%) simulating enterprise automation, Vending-Bench 2 ($16,843) simulating long-term business operations, RiemannBench (84.0%) for scientific reasoning, and the output presentation quality item of AA-Briefcase (1771 Elo); the cybersecurity-specialized version open to Fairwind program defenders also scored a high of 90.5% on SEC-bench Pro.

However, this new engine is not without flaws.

The first problem is the "verbosity" and latency issue under high tiers. When running the full AA evaluation in xhigh mode, Neon output a total of 283 million tokens, much more than Carbon, and the first response latency also reached 56.51 seconds. For scenarios that pursue extreme response speed, it is obviously wiser to switch it back to medium mode: the time consumption can be reduced to 8.3 minutes, and the output volume will also converge to 62.9 million tokens.

Another episode that developers on the domestic tech forum "Da Lao Shuo" talked about with relish is the brief "price inversion" that appeared before the end of November.

Neon's API was launched directly at the official price of $3 for input and $15 for output (per million tokens, with a 95% discount to $0.15 for cache hits), with no free quota provided; while the flagship Carbon and Argon happened to be in their launch promotion periods of $2 and $10 before November 30, and will not return to the original prices of $4 and $20 until December 1. This means that in the remaining ten-odd days of November, the unit price of the sub-flagship is 50% more expensive than the flagship, which is a slightly humorous commercial time difference.

## 02

## From Solo Stunt Show to Contractor Leading the Team

Benchmark tables are static after all, and what really excites the tech circle is the dominance that Neon demonstrates in real engineering environments.

When you open the real machine demo screen of Google Antigravity, you can intuitively feel what long-range multi-agent collaboration is.

In a project called NEONPUTT 84, Neon starts the /swarm mode, and simultaneously schedules 8 parallel nodes including scaffold, shaders, courses, physics, ui, engine, verifier in the real-time beating task graph. They divided the work to write custom GLSL shaders, a 240Hz physics engine and 8 levels, and built a mini golf game full of 3D synthetic wave style. What's even more amazing is that after writing the code, it took over the browser to click the test interface by itself, aimed, hit the ball, and steadily made a hole in one.
