Kimi.content:
# 快速开始

Source: https://platform.kimi.com/docs/get-api-key

从创建 API Key 到完成第一次 Kimi API 调用。

你可以通过 Kimi API 调用 Kimi K3.1 Pro 等模型。调用时，可以选择 Chat Completions API、Responses API 或 Messages API。创建 API Key、选择模型并配置base_url 后，即可直接通过 HTTP 发送请求，或使用 OpenAI SDK、Anthropic SDK 发起调用。

[!NOTE]

Kimi K3.1 Pro 普速版和高速版已发布！作为 Kimi 迄今为止能力最强的旗舰模型，K3.1 Pro 支持 1M token 上下文与原生视觉理解，在代码、3D 创作、金融研究与建模等方面的能力得到显著提升，适合 Kimi Code、Codex、Claude Code 等编程 Agent 以及知识工作与深度推理场景。加入 Kimi 开发者交流群，let’s build with Kimi!

## 开始使用

1. 获取 API Key

访问 Kimi API 开放平台 ，登录后进入 API Keys 页面创建并复制 API Key。

请妥善保管你的 API Key，不要泄露给他人，也不要直接硬编码在代码中。建议使用环境变量保存：
export MOONSHOT_API_KEY="你的_KIMI_API_KEY"

[card] Kimi API 开放平台

登录开放平台，进入控制台、开发工作台和用户中心。

[card] API Keys

创建、复制和管理用于 API 调用的密钥。

2. 选择模型

作为快速开始入口，建议优先从 Kimi K3.1 Pro 开始；追求更高输出速度时可选择 Kimi K3.1 Pro 高速版。

[card] Kimi K3.1 Pro
kimi-k3.1-pro 是全新 K3.1 系列的首个旗舰模型——3 万亿级参数、1M token 上下文，代码、3D 创作、金融研究与建模能力显著提升。
[card] Kimi K3.1 Pro 高速版
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed 是 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的高速版，能力相同、约为 2～3 倍速度，适合对输出速度要求更高的场景。
3. 选择调用方式

Kimi API 兼容 OpenAI 与 Anthropic API 格式，你可以根据项目技术栈选择最合适的接入方式。

[card] Chat Completions API

OpenAI 兼容格式，支持 OpenAI SDK 与任意语言 HTTP 接入。

[card] Responses API

OpenAI 兼容格式，生成文本/JSON 输出或调用函数工具。

[card] Messages API

Anthropic 兼容格式，适合 Anthropic SDK、Claude Code 等工具接入。

[card] 开发工作台

无需写代码，快速测试提示词、模型效果和业务样例。

4. 发起第一次调用

请将第 1 步创建的 API Key 设置为MOONSHOT_API_KEY 环境变量，示例会通过该变量读取密钥。

运行示例前，请准备：

- Python 3.9 及以上版本，或 Node.js 18 及以上版本。
- OpenAI SDK 1.0.0 及以上版本。Kimi API 兼容 OpenAI API 格式，你可以直接使用 Python 或 Node.js OpenAI SDK 进行调用。pip install --upgrade 'openai>=1.0' # Python
npm install openai@latest # Node.js

[tab] python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["MOONSHOT_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://api.moonshot.cn/v1",
)

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "你是 Kimi，由 Moonshot AI 提供的人工智能助手，你更擅长中文和英文的对话。你会为用户提供安全，有帮助，准确的回答。同时，你会拒绝一切涉及恐怖主义，种族歧视，黄色暴力等问题的回答。Moonshot AI 为专有名词，不可翻译成其他语言。"},
        {"role": "user", "content": "你好，我叫李雷，1+1等于多少？"}
    ]
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

[tab] curl
curl https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOONSHOT_API_KEY" \
    -d '{
        "model": "kimi-k3.1-pro",
        "messages": [
            {"role": "system", "content": "你是 Kimi，由 Moonshot AI 提供的人工智能助手，你更擅长中文和英文的对话。你会为用户提供安全，有帮助，准确的回答。同时，你会拒绝一切涉及恐怖主义，种族歧视，黄色暴力等问题的回答。Moonshot AI 为专有名词，不可翻译成其他语言。"},
            {"role": "user", "content": "你好，我叫李雷，1+1等于多少？"}
        ]
   }'

[tab] node.js
const OpenAI = require("openai");

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.MOONSHOT_API_KEY,
  baseURL: "https://api.moonshot.cn/v1",
});

async function main() {
  const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({
    model: "kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages: [
      {"role": "system", "content": "你是 Kimi，由 Moonshot AI 提供的人工智能助手，你更擅长中文和英文的对话。你会为用户提供安全，有帮助，准确的回答。同时，你会拒绝一切涉及恐怖主义，种族歧视，黄色暴力等问题的回答。Moonshot AI 为专有名词，不可翻译成其他语言。"},
      {"role": "user", "content": "你好，我叫李雷，1+1等于多少？"}
    ]
  });

  console.log(completion.choices[0].message.content);
}

main();

如果成功运行上述代码，且没有任何报错，你将看到类似如下的内容输出：
你好，李雷！1+1 等于 2。这是一个基本的数学加法问题。如果你有其他问题或需要帮助，请随时告诉我。

注：由于 Kimi 大模型的不确定性，实际的回复内容可能并不与上述内容完全一致。

## 模型参数补充说明

本页示例默认使用最新模型kimi-k3.1-pro。K3.1 Pro 使用请求顶层 reasoning_effort 配置推理强度（支持 "low" / "high" / "max"，默认 "max"）。换用 kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed 等其他模型时，需要替换 model 字段，并根据模型支持情况调整参数配置，详见模型参数参考。

## 探索更多功能

[card] 流式输出

启用
stream，让回复边生成边返回，适合聊天、代码生成和长文本输出场景。
[card] 多轮对话

通过维护
messages 列表实现上下文记忆，让模型记住对话历史。
[card] 多模态输入

Kimi K3.1 Pro 和 Kimi K3 均支持文本、图片与视频输入。

[card] 工具调用

让模型调用外部函数或 API，实现 Agent 任务、联网搜索和复杂工作流。

[card] JSON Mode

强制模型输出合法 JSON，方便结构化数据提取和下游系统对接。

[card] 思考模型

使用思考能力处理复杂推理、多步工具调用和 Agent 任务。

## 相关资源

查看 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的模型能力、调用示例和最佳实践。

[card] Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed

查看 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed 的模型定价。

提供建议、问题反馈、分享案例: Let's Build with Kimi !

查看当前可用模型名称和模型说明。

cache_control：默认按 5m TTL 读写缓存；发生缓存写入时，按 5m 档计费。{
    "model": "kimi-k3.1-pro",
    "cache_control": { "type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h" },
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "你好"}]
}

行为说明

- 缓存以组织（org）为粒度隔离，组织之间不共享缓存。

- 相同前缀的请求在缓存有效期内命中后，缓存的有效期会按原 TTL 刷新；命中部分只收取缓存读取费用，不再收取缓存写入费用。

- 缓存写入按 TTL 分别计费，价格详见产品定价。

- 不支持手动清除缓存，已缓存的前缀在至少 5 分钟不活动后自动过期。

说明

Kimi.description: Kimi API 提供以程式方式存取 Moonshot AI 的 Kimi 模型，讓開發人員可將文字生成、多輪對話、程式設計輔助、文件分析和視覺理解整合至應用程式中 ... Kimi API 平台可讓您存取 Moonshot AI 的 Kimi 模型...
Kimi.content:
閱讀時長：12分鐘更新於：2026-11-16

AI 正在改變開發人員建置應用程式、自動化任務及提供更智慧數位體驗的方式。模型 API 讓您無須從頭開發模型，即可將先進的 AI 功能整合至軟體中。Kimi API 為開發人員提供強大的語言模型，可用於文字生成、程式設計、推理及文件分析。本指南將介紹 Kimi API、其主要功能、實際應用，以及如何開始使用。

## 什麼是模型 API

模型 API 是讓應用程式透過程式碼存取 AI 模型的介面。應用程式會傳送包含文字或圖片等輸入內容的結構化請求，並接收模型生成的結果。託管式模型 API 讓開發人員無須自行訓練或營運底層模型，即可使用這些功能。

Kimi API 提供以程式方式存取 Moonshot AI 的 Kimi 模型，讓開發人員可將文字生成、多輪對話、程式設計輔助、文件分析和視覺理解整合至應用程式中。

透過統一介面，開發人員可將 AI 模型連接至網站、軟體應用程式、內部工具及自動化工作流程。這能簡化 AI 整合，並免除管理底層模型基礎設施的需求。

### AI 模型 API 的類型

AI 模型 API 可支援不同類型的輸入與任務，具體取決於底層模型及其功能。常見類別包括：

文字生成 API：根據使用者提示詞生成、改寫、翻譯及摘要文字。常用於聊天機器人、寫作助理及內容創作應用程式。

嵌入 API：將文字或其他支援的資料轉換為數值向量表示。開發人員可使用這些嵌入資料進行語意搜尋、推薦系統及檢索增強生成（RAG）。

圖片生成 API：根據文字提示詞或參考圖片生成或編輯圖片，支援設計工具和創意平台等應用程式。

多模態 API：在同一次互動中處理文字和圖片等多種類型的輸入。這些 API 可支援視覺問答、圖片分析及其他多模態應用程式。

語音與音訊 API：將語音轉換為文字、生成語音音訊，或處理語音輸入，以支援語音助理和轉錄工具等應用程式。

部分 AI 模型支援多種功能，因此這些類別並非互斥。例如，支援的 Kimi 模型可處理文字型任務和視覺輸入，讓開發人員能建置結合語言理解與圖片分析的應用程式。

## 模型 API 在 AI 平台中的角色

模型 API 是應用程式用來呼叫 AI 模型的介面。AI API 平台除了提供這些介面外，也提供管理 API 金鑰、帳務、使用量及相關服務的工具。平台可能提供自有模型、第三方模型，或兩者兼具。

例如，Kimi API 平台可讓您存取 Moonshot AI 的 Kimi 模型，並提供用於建立金鑰和監控使用量的主控台。開發人員從應用程式呼叫模型 API，並透過平台管理該存取權限。兩者在同一開發工作流程中搭配運作。

## 為何使用 Kimi API

存取 Kimi 的先進模型：Kimi API 讓開發人員可存取 Moonshot AI 的最新模型，包括專為複雜推理、程式設計及多模態任務設計的先進模型。這些模型具備更強的問題解決能力、更出色的程式碼生成能力及長上下文理解能力，協助開發人員建置可處理複雜指令、分析大量資訊及管理高要求工作流程的應用程式。

相容 OpenAI 的 API 格式：Kimi API 支援 OpenAI Chat Completions API 格式，讓開發人員可使用相容的 OpenAI SDK。設定 Kimi API 基礎 URL、API 金鑰和模型 ID 後，在調整既有應用程式前，請先確認支援的參數及模型專屬行為。這項相容性讓您更容易將 AI 模型 API 整合至既有的開發工作流程。

串流與非串流回應：Kimi API 同時支援串流與非串流回應模式，以因應不同的應用程式需求。非串流請求會傳回完整回應，而串流則透過伺服器傳送事件（SSE）逐步傳遞生成內容。

這種彈性讓模型 API 適用於背景處理，也適用於需要即時回饋的互動式聊天應用程式。

彈性整合：開發人員可將 Kimi API 連接至網站、後端服務、自訂應用程式及自動化工作流程。其以 API 為基礎的架構，可彈性地將模型 API 功能納入不同技術環境與開發專案。

## 如何開始使用 Kimi API

開始使用 Kimi API 有多種方式，取決於您想使用 Kimi 自有的開發工具，還是要將其模型整合至既有應用程式。您可以將 Kimi API 連接至 Kimi Code CLI 以進行 AI 輔助軟體開發，也可以使用相容的 SDK 和工具建置自己的應用程式。

### 搭配 Kimi Code 使用 Kimi API

Kimi Code CLI 是以終端機為基礎的 AI 程式設計 agent，可讀取及修改專案檔案、執行指令、分析程式碼，並協助完成軟體開發任務。您可使用 API 金鑰將其連接至 Kimi Platform API，並直接在開發環境中使用 Kimi 模型。

步驟 1：建立 Kimi API 帳戶

前往 Kimi API 平台並註冊帳戶。登入後即可存取開發人員主控台，在其中管理 API 金鑰及檢視 API 使用量。累計儲值達5 優惠券（開始呼叫 API 前，最低儲值金額為 $1）。目前條款請查看儲值政策及主控台。5時，您將獲得一張5 時，您將獲得一張 

步驟 2：產生 API 金鑰

在主控台中開啟 API 金鑰管理區段，並建立新的 API 金鑰。

複製產生的金鑰並妥善安全保存。請避免將其硬編碼至應用程式中，或暴露於用戶端程式碼內。

步驟 3：安裝 Kimi Code CLI

Kimi Code CLI 是支援 Kimi Platform API、以終端機為基礎的 AI 程式設計 agent。

在 macOS 或 Linux 上，請使用官方安裝指令碼進行安裝：

curl -fsSL https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.sh | bash

在 Windows 上，開啟 PowerShell 並執行：

irm https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.ps1 | iex

在 Windows 上啟動 Kimi Code CLI 前，請確認已安裝 Git for Windows。

或者，也可透過 npm 安裝：

npm install -g @moonshot-ai/kimi-code

透過 npm 安裝需要 Node.js 22.19.0 或更新版本。

步驟 4：將 Kimi API 連接至 Kimi Code

前往專案目錄並啟動 Kimi Code CLI：

cd your-project kimi

在 Kimi Code CLI 的互動式介面中輸入/login。選取 Kimi Platform API key，然後貼上先前建立的 API 金鑰。

本範例在 Kimi Code CLI 中使用 Kimi Platform API 金鑰。使用量會依適用的 token 費率計入您的 API 帳戶，與 Kimi Code 訂閱方案的額度分開計費。如需目前的安裝與驗證選項，請參閱 Kimi Code CLI 快速入門指南。

步驟 5：選擇模型並開始編碼

在 Kimi Code CLI 中輸入/model 開啟模型選擇器，並選擇可用模型。

選定模型後，請在 CLI 中輸入編碼任務。例如：

檢視專案結構、找出潛在問題，並提出程式碼庫的改善建議。

接著，Kimi Code 可協助檢查專案檔案、分析程式碼、提出修改建議，以及協助處理開發工作。

### 將 Kimi API 整合至其他 SDK 與工具

如果您正在建置自己的應用程式，或已使用 AI 開發框架，也可以透過相容的 SDK 與工具整合 Kimi 模型，而非使用 Kimi Code CLI。

Kimi API 支援 OpenAI API 格式，因此使用 OpenAI Python 或 Node.js SDK 的應用程式，通常只要更新 API 基礎 URL、API 金鑰與模型 ID 即可連線。例如，使用 OpenAI Python SDK：

步驟 1：安裝 OpenAI SDK

pip install openai

步驟 2：設定 Kimi API 用戶端

在將用來執行 Python 的終端機中，將 API 金鑰設為環境變數。在 macOS 或 Linux 上：

export MOONSHOT_API_KEY="YOUR_KIMI_API_KEY"

在 Windows PowerShell 上：

$env:MOONSHOT_API_KEY="YOUR_KIMI_API_KEY"

接著在 Python 中建立用戶端：

import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( api_key=os.environ["MOONSHOT_API_KEY"], base_url="https://api.moonshot.ai/v1" )

本範例使用國際版 API 端點。如果您使用中國大陸平台，請依照該平台的文件使用https://api.moonshot.cn/v1，並採用該平台的 API 金鑰與可用模型。請依據您的平台帳戶與憑證選擇端點，而非僅依實際所在地切換。

步驟 3：向 Kimi 模型傳送請求

response = client.chat.completions.create( model="kimi-k3.1-pro", messages=[ { "role": "user", "content": "說明 Python 裝飾器的運作方式。" } ] ) print(response.choices[0].message.content)

本範例使用 Chat Completions 介面向 Kimi K3.1 Pro 傳送訊息，並列印產生的回應。您可透過串流、工具呼叫及其他支援的 API 功能擴充整合。

其他 SDK 與開發工具

除了 OpenAI SDK 外，Kimi API 也可與其他相容用戶端及 AI 編碼工具整合。例如，開發者可使用 Anthropic SDK 搭配 Anthropic Messages API 格式，或設定 Claude Code、Codex、OpenClaw 等工具及其他相容 agent，使其搭配 Kimi 模型運作。

設定流程會因工具而異。視整合方式而定，您可能需要指定 API 金鑰、基礎 URL、模型 ID 與 API 通訊協定。設定連線前，請查閱相關工具文件及 Kimi 的 API 相容性指南。

如需更多資訊，請參閱 Kimi API 文件與模型清單。

## 如何為應用程式選擇 Kimi 模型

選擇 Kimi 模型時，需要在任務品質、輸出速度與整體 API 成本之間取得平衡。請先以應用程式中具代表性的任務測試模型，再比較其結果與 token 用量。

下表概述各模型適合考慮的情境：

模型 | 建議工作負載 | 選擇理由 
---|---|---
kimi-k3.1-pro | 新應用程式、複雜程式設計、研究，以及長期執行的 agent 任務 | 適合新專案的實用起點，在這三款模型中具有最低的標準輸入與輸出費率。 
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed | 互動式程式設計，以及使用者等待生成輸出的其他工作流程 | 具備與 K3.1 Pro 相同的模型能力，但輸出生成速度約快 2–3 倍。標準輸入、輸出及快取寫入費率較高。 
kimi-k3 | 已使用 K3 測試的既有應用程式 | 適合維護已驗證 K3 整合的選項；切換前，請先以自身任務評估較新的模型。 

### Kimi API 定價

以下費率適用於國際版 API 平台，並以每百萬 token（1,000,000 token）的美元價格，未含適用稅金列示。三個模型皆支援 1,048,576 token 的上下文視窗。

模型 | 未快取輸入 | 輸出 | 快取命中 | 快取寫入（5 分鐘） | 快取寫入（1 小時） 
---|---|---|---|---|---
kimi-k3.1-pro | $2.00 | $10.00 | $0.20 | $2.00 | $4.00 
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed | $4.00 | $20.00 | $0.20 | $4.00 | $8.00 
kimi-k3 | $3.00 | $15.00 | $0.30 | $3.00 | $6.00 

本指南使用的 Chat Completions 介面中，輸入 token 分為三種互斥的計費類別：未快取輸入、快取命中與快取寫入。計為快取寫入的 token，不會同時按未快取輸入費率收費。估算成本時，請使用 API 回報的用量明細。

自動快取預設會為符合資格的前綴使用 5 分鐘 TTL；也提供 1 小時 TTL。快取命中會按快取命中費率計費，並延長現有 TTL，不會再次收取寫入費用。請查看官方 API 定價頁面與上下文快取指南，以取得目前的費率與計費規則。

為應用程式選擇模型時，請考量以下因素：

任務品質：新專案可先從 K3.1 Pro 開始，再測試是否符合您的準確性與可靠性需求。若您現有的整合採用 K3，請先在自己的迴歸測試中比較行為，再進行切換。

輸入模態：三個模型皆支援原生視覺理解。請確認所選模型支援的輸入格式，以及工作流程所需的前處理要求。

上下文長度：三者皆提供 100 萬 token 的上下文視窗。視窗大小本身無法區分它們；也請評估檢索品質、延遲，以及處理長篇歷史內容的成本。

輸出速度：若較快的生成速度很重要，請考慮 K3.1 Pro Highspeed。其輸出速度約為 2–3×，但不應視為保證每項端對端任務都能快 2–3× 完成。

總用量與成本：比較未快取輸入、快取讀取與寫入、輸出用量，以及任何付費工具。在此比較中，K3.1 Pro 的標準輸入與輸出費率最低。應根據回報的用量（包括推理 token）估算輸出成本，而非僅依最終答案的長度估算。

如需目前的模型 ID 與功能，請參閱 Kimi API 模型清單。在選擇正式環境模型前，請先針對自己的工作負載測試候選模型。

## Kimi API 的常見使用案例

Kimi API 支援多種開發情境，涵蓋對話式應用程式、內容生成、文件分析及多模態工作流程。開發者可將 Kimi 模型整合至既有產品，或建置新的 AI 驅動應用程式，以完成以下任務：

AI 客服與對話式助理：將 Kimi API 整合至客服平台、聊天機器人與虛擬助理，以回答問題、說明產品細節並處理常見支援請求。只要在新的 API 請求中加入先前訊息，應用程式即可維持對話脈絡並提供更貼切的回覆。這使 Kimi API 適用於客服自動化、互動式學習工具、個人化推薦及其他對話式應用程式。

AI 寫作與內容生成：建置可根據使用者指示與上下文資訊生成自然語言內容的寫作助理和內容創作工具。開發者可使用 Kimi 模型建立文章、產品說明與行銷文案，也可改寫、翻譯及摘要文字。這些功能也能支援寫作與生產力應用程式中的問答、脈絡化說明及資訊擷取。

文件分析與知識檢索：將 Kimi 模型整合至文件處理工作流程，以分析冗長資料、摘要報告、擷取研究發現，並回答與提供內容相關的問題。開發者也可結合長上下文處理與文件檢索系統，建置能處理多來源資訊的知識型應用程式。潛在應用包括研究論文分析、內部知識搜尋、文件問答及資訊整理。

AI 程式設計助理與開發工具：使用 Kimi API 支援程式碼生成、除錯、程式碼說明及技術文件等軟體開發任務。開發者可將模型回應整合至程式碼編輯器、開發平台及內部工程工具。結合函式呼叫後，Kimi 模型也能與外部開發服務和函式互動，為程式設計助理及更進階的 AI 驅動開發工作流程奠定基礎。

多模態應用程式：使用支援的 Kimi 模型，搭配文字提示詞處理視覺輸入，讓應用程式能夠理解圖片與影片，並回應自然語言指示。開發者可結合文字與視覺理解，建置影像問答、視覺內容分析、圖片與影片理解，以及其他涉及多種輸入類型的工作流程。支援的輸入格式與功能取決於所選模型。

## 結語

總而言之，Kimi API 讓開發者無須從頭建置模型，也能更輕鬆地將進階 AI 功能整合至應用程式。從內容生成和文件分析，到程式設計與多模態任務，皆能支援各類開發需求。透過靈活的 AI 模型 API，您可以選擇合適的模型，建置實用的 AI 驅動應用程式。

## 常見問題

模型 API 透過結構化請求，將您的應用程式連接至 AI 模型。您的應用程式會將提示詞或圖片等輸入傳送至 API 端點，模型處理後會傳回可供軟體使用的回應。

可以，Kimi API 可透過模型互動與工具呼叫支援 AI agent 開發。開發人員可將 Kimi 模型連接至外部函式、資料庫和服務，建置能執行任務、擷取資訊及支援自動化工作流程的 agent。

429 回應通常表示請求超出適用的速率限制或配額。請在主控台查看錯誤詳情，以及帳戶的 API 使用量與限制。若為暫時性的速率限制，請降低並行數或請求頻率，並依照回應中的任何重試指引採用指數退避策略。若使用配額已耗盡，請先處理該限制再重試。詳情請參閱速率限制文件。

Kimi.content:
# Kimi K3.1 Pro

Source: https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart

了解 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的 API 调用方式：推理强度、流式输出、视觉输入、工具调用与 100 万 token 上下文。

## 模型简介

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是全新 K3.1 系列的第一个模型，也是我们迄今能力最强的 3 万亿级参数模型，支持 100 万上下文。K3.1 Pro 在代码、3D 创作、金融研究和其他长程 Agent 能力上的提升尤为显著。

我们同步推出高速版模型 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed，同等智能，输出速度约 2~3 倍。完整模型权重将于 11 月 4 日前发布。

### 持续突破前沿

在 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的研发中，我们大幅增加了强化学习（RL）环节的算力投入。为了支撑数百个下游领域的大规模联合训练，我们优化了技术栈的每一层，包括 RL 框架、长上下文推理、训练效率、沙箱基础设施、调度系统，以及用于环境质量检查的共享平台等，确保每一份新增的 RL 算力都能转化为稳定、高效的回报。

在代码、Agent 和知识类基准上，K3.1 Pro 达到或接近最强闭源模型的水平。Terminal-Bench 4.0 通过真实环境中资源受限的终端任务考察编程智能体的能力，每项任务均设有严格的专项测试。K3.1 Pro 在此项评估中得分 65.7%，超过 GPT-6 Astra（58.2%），与 Claude Opus 5.5（66.4%）仅有微弱差距。Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 是我们内部的基准测试，覆盖多种工程领域，重点考察编程智能体的多步执行、工具调用和端到端问题解决能力。K3.1 Pro 在此项测试中得分 61.2%，高于 K3 的 55.95%。

快速开始

### 代码

各种规模的编码任务，Kimi K3.1 Pro 都能完成：小到在真实代码库里修复一个问题，大到从零搭建一个完整项目。它也为游戏和网页体验带来更考究的视觉风格，并且知道如何用合适的外部专业工具把它们做出来。

K3.1 Pro 能熟练使用 Unity、Unreal Engine、Godot 等游戏引擎，并结合网络搜索与 3D 生成，做出完整的体验。它产出的前端页面、Three.js 交互场景和 3D 资产，在构图、排版、动效和细节打磨上都有明显提升。以下案例均由 K3.1 Pro 端到端完成：

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Unreal Engine 5.8 中构建了一座神话般的东方天宫，其特色在于一个半径为 1,750 米的、拥有 36 个柱间的柱廊——该柱廊在 Blender 中通过程序化建模生成，并通过 Nanite 和 Lumen 渲染了 3,600 万个源三角形。使用的外部资源包括：Cloud Forge VDB 云、Poly Haven/ambientCG 8K 材质，以及 NASA LRO/LOLA 月球数据。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Unreal Engine 5.8 制作了一段以东方古代为主题的 3D 角色扮演游戏预告片，片中一名剑客穿梭于云海之中，掠过漂浮的岛屿，最终进入云端之上的一座古典城市。概念设计及部分资源灵感源自Rednote创作者@-Duduu-。使用的外部资源：犍陀罗佛像和水月观音的3D扫描数据（明尼阿波利斯艺术博物馆，CC0）。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Godot 4.7.2 制作了一款风格独特的 3D 动作冒险游戏。该项目包含五个可探索区域，拥有程序生成的地形、道路、水域、植被和村庄布局，同时具备第三人称战斗、两阶段的BOSS战、资源采集、昼夜循环以及篝火快速传送功能。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 开发了一个基于浏览器的 3D 机械臂展示系统，其中包含爆炸图、透明外壳和剖面图。该系统通过代码生成了 2,317 个部件和 268 条动态布线路径，并已通过 55 项浏览器验证。

### 3D 建模

Kimi K3.1 Pro 模型擅长 3D 创作与空间推理。给它一段文字描述、一张草图或一张参考图，它能推断出物体的形状、比例和空间关系，并将其重建为可用的 3D 模型。Kimi K3.1 Pro 可以不依赖 MCP 连接器，直接编写并运行 Blender、SolidWorks、Rhino 等专业建模软件脚本，完成素材构建、几何与材质细化、场景搭建，最后将成果接入 Three.js 场景或游戏引擎。

K3.1 Pro 擅长参数化建模，例如机械零件、建筑模型、多参数可配置的产品和定制家具。无需依赖 MCP 连接器，它可以直接编写并运行 Blender、CAD 等专业建模工具的脚本，完成素材的构建与细化，修改单个部件，并调整几何、材质与场景布局。

以下案例均由 Kimi K3.1 Pro 端到端完成，可直接用于品牌宣传片、游戏和交互式网页体验。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Blender 中构建了一个机场内的热带雨林山谷，并制作了一段时长 17.5 秒、分辨率为 1920×1080、帧率为 60 fps 的建模展示视频。 使用的工具：Blender、Python、Geometry Nodes、Cycles、Pillow、NumPy 和 FFmpeg。 使用的外部资源：来自 Poly Haven 的“Kloofendal 48d Partly Cloudy (Pure Sky)” 4K HDRI 素材，作者为 Greg Zaal 和 Jarod Guest，采用 CC0 许可，用于天空照明和环境反射。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Python 在 FreeCAD 中构建了一个详细的涡扇发动机模型，涵盖了风扇、减速齿轮箱、压缩机、燃烧室、涡轮以及外部管道，共计 2,100 个实体。该项目支持分步装配、内部爆炸图，以及展示风扇、低压转子和高压转子分别以 2,780、8,590 和 12,400 RPM 转速运行的旋转动画。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 利用 Trimesh 技术，设计了一款由五部分组成的、可 3D 打印的台灯，其灵感源自福建土楼，将土楼独特的圆形建筑结构重新诠释为精致的镂空格栅。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Blender 中构建了一个基于浏览器的交互式 3D 网页，创建了一座由约 330 万个三角面组成的教堂内部场景，并为 8,368 个组件添加了动画效果，其中包括肋拱穹顶、石雕以及生动逼真的彩色玻璃光影效果。使用的外部资源：来自 Poly Haven 的石材纹理（CC0）以及 Mylius 拍摄的彩绘玻璃照片（CC BY-SA 3.0）。

快速开始

### 金融

凭借更强的推理与工具调用能力，Kimi K3.1 Pro 能够端到端交付完整的金融工作流。在外部基准上，K3.1 Pro 在 Office QA Pro v2 和 SpreadsheetBench 2 上均取得最佳成绩，两项均超过 Opus 5.5、Fable 5.1 和 GPT 6 Astra。Office QA Pro v2 考察基于真实金融文档的复杂财务数据分析，涉及检索、跨文档核对与多步数值推理；SpreadsheetBench 2 评估端到端的电子表格工作流，包括财务建模、跨表公式依赖与错误诊断。在衡量完整投资工作流（从标的筛选到盈利能力分析）的 Frontier Finance 上，K3.1 Pro 相比 K3 也有提升。

金融分析和投资研究对事实准确性有很高要求。为此，我们针对高难度真实工作场景和高难度提示词，对 K3.1 Pro 的事实准确性进行了专项优化。在用户标记过事实错误的一组去标识化对话测试中，相较于 k3，新模型的单项事实陈述错误率从 23.35% 降至 6.85%；包含至少一处事实错误的回答比例仅为前代的约 46.4%。（这是一项针对事实准确性的压力测试，样本刻意聚焦模型容易出错的情形，所报告的错误率不代表日常使用中的整体水平。）

## 访问条件

调用前请确保账户有可用余额。在开放平台完成充值（最低充值金额 10 元）后即可解锁调用。新用户注册并完成认证后获赠的 15 元代金券可用于 Kimi K3.1 Pro；高速版 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed 不适用。代金券规则详见 账号与财务。

累计充值金额同时决定账户等级与速率限制（并发、RPM、TPM、TPD），详见 充值与限速 。

## 立即开始

以下示例需要 Python 3.9+ 和 OpenAI SDK。先安装 SDK，并初始化一次客户端；后续 Python 示例复用client。
python3 -m pip install --upgrade 'openai>=1.0'
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["MOONSHOT_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://api.moonshot.cn/v1",
)

## 基础调用

[!NOTE]

K3.1 Pro 提供高速版本
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed，模型 ID 与价格见 产品定价 。
[tab] Python
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "用一句话介绍 Kimi K3.1 Pro。"}],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

[tab] cURL
curl https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/chat/completions \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $MOONSHOT_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "model": "kimi-k3.1-pro",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "用一句话介绍 Kimi K3.1 Pro。"}]
  }'

## 推理强度

K3.1 Pro 始终开启思考模式，并支持通过请求顶层reasoning_effort 配置推理强度。推理强度支持 low / high / max 三档（默认 max）。用法见 推理强度 。
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    reasoning_effort="max",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "证明根号 2 是无理数。"}],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

多轮对话和工具调用时，将 API 返回的完整 assistant message 原样加入下一次请求，不要只保留content。

## 流式输出

流式响应分别提供推理增量reasoning_content 和最终答案增量 content。更多细节见 流式输出 。
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "解释为什么天空是蓝色的。"}],
    stream=True,
)

for chunk in stream:
    delta = chunk.choices[0].delta
    reasoning = getattr(delta, "reasoning_content", None)
    if reasoning:
        print(reasoning, end="", flush=True)
    if delta.content:
        print(delta.content, end="", flush=True)

## 视觉输入

视觉消息的content 必须是对象数组，而不是序列化后的字符串。完整格式与限制见 视觉输入 。

[tab] 本地图片
import base64
from pathlib import Path

image_data: str = base64.b64encode(Path("image.png").read_bytes()).decode()
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "image_url",
                    "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{image_data}"},
                },
                {"type": "text", "text": "描述这张图片。"},
            ],
        }
    ],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

[tab] 视频文件
from pathlib import Path

video = client.files.create(file=Path("video.mp4"), purpose="video")
try:
    completion = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
        messages=[
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "video_url",
                        "video_url": {"url": f"ms://{video.id}"},
                    },
                    {"type": "text", "text": "概括这个视频。"},
                ],
            }
        ],
    )
    print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
finally:
    client.files.delete(video.id)

## 结构化输出

使用json_schema 和 strict: true 约束最终 message.content，只解析该字段，不解析 reasoning_content。

[accordion] 姓名与年龄 schema
import json

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "小林今年 28 岁。提取姓名和年龄。"}
    ],
    response_format={
        "type": "json_schema",
        "json_schema": {
            "name": "person",
            "strict": True,
            "schema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "name": {"type": "string"},
                    "age": {"type": "integer"},
                },
                "required": ["name", "age"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
)

person: dict[str, object] = json.loads(
    completion.choices[0].message.content or "{}"
)
print(person)

详见 结构化输出 。

## Partial Mode

在消息末尾添加partial=True 的 assistant message，让模型从指定文本前缀继续生成。最终展示时需要自行拼接前缀。
prefix: str = "结论："
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "用一句话说明保持接口兼容的重要性。"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": prefix, "partial": True},
    ],
)

print(prefix + (completion.choices[0].message.content or ""))

详见 Partial Mode 。

## 自定义工具与tool_choice

首轮用tool_choice="required" 强制至少调用一个工具。执行每个调用后，回传完整 assistant message，并用对应的 tool_call_id 逐条追加工具结果。

[accordion] 最小天气 Agent Loop
import json
from typing import Any

tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "get_weather",
            "description": "查询城市天气",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["city"],
            },
        },
    }
]
messages: list[Any] = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "北京今天天气怎么样？"}
]

first = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=messages,
    tools=tools,
    tool_choice="required",
)
assistant_message = first.choices[0].message
messages.append(assistant_message)

for tool_call in assistant_message.tool_calls or []:
    arguments: dict[str, str] = json.loads(tool_call.function.arguments)
    result: str = json.dumps(
        {"city": arguments["city"], "weather": "晴", "temperature_c": 24},
        ensure_ascii=False,
    )
    messages.append(
        {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tool_call.id, "content": result}
    )

final = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=messages,
    tools=tools,
)
print(final.choices[0].message.content)

详见 工具调用约束 。

把完整工具定义放进一条不含content 的 system message，即可从该位置起加载工具。

When consuming on-demand throughput on thebedrock-mantle endpoint, available throughput scales over time. Not all requests within your quota are guaranteed to succeed during periods of high demand, so ramping gradually is important. For this model, default limits aren't surfaced directly through Service Quotas, so we recommend following the ramp as your guide.

## Sample Code

Step 1 - AWS Account: If you have an AWS account already, skip this step. If you are new to AWS, sign up for an AWS account.

Step 2 - API key: Go to the Amazon Bedrock console and generate a long-term API key.

Step 3 - Get the SDK: To use this getting started guide, you must have Python already installed. Then install the relevant software depending on the APIs you are using.

Chat Completions API
pip install openai

Responses API
pip install openai

Step 4 - Set environment variables: Configure your environment to use the API key for authentication.

Chat Completions API
OPENAI_API_KEY="<provide your Bedrock API key>"
OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://bedrock-mantle.us-west-2.api.aws/openai/v1"

Responses API
OPENAI_API_KEY="<provide your Bedrock API key>"
OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://bedrock-mantle.us-west-2.api.aws/openai/v1"

Step 5 - Run your first inference request: Save the file asbedrock-first-request.py

Chat Completions API
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="xai.grok-4.3",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"}
    ]
)
print(response)

Responses API
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="xai.grok-4.3",
    input="Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"
)
print(response)

## Usage Considerations and Limitations

Reasoning effort — Reasoning is always active by default. You can configure effort through thereasoning parameter: {"effort": "none"} (disables reasoning), "low" (default), "medium", or "high". Reasoning content is encrypted and can be returned by passing include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"] in the Responses API request. You can send the encrypted content back in subsequent turns to provide reasoning context for multi-turn conversations. The Chat Completions API does not return reasoning tokens.
response = client.responses.create(
    model="xai.grok-4.3",
    reasoning={"effort": "high"},
    include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"],
    input="Explain quantum entanglement simply."
)
print(response.output_text)

- Default parameters — Grok 4.3 uses defaults that differ from the standard OpenAI API specification:temperature defaults to 0.7 (not 1), top_p defaults to 0.95 (not 1), and max_completion_tokens defaults to 131072. Adjust these values explicitly if your application requires different behavior.

Document Conventions

Grok 4.6

Z.AI

Did this page help you? - Yes

Thanks for letting us know we're doing a good job!

If you've got a moment, please tell us what we did right so we can do more of it.

Did this page help you? - No

Thanks for letting us know this page needs work. We're sorry we let you down.

If you've got a moment, please tell us how we can make the documentation better.

xAI.content:
# xAI (Grok)

Thexai provider supports xAI's Grok models through an API interface compatible with OpenAI's format, including text, vision, image generation, video generation, and voice workflows.

## Setup

To use xAI's API, set theXAI_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file.
export XAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

When xAI is the selected fallback provider family, Promptfoo can use xAI defaults for grading, suggestions, synthesis, and web search. These automatic defaults currently usegrok-4.3 on the global endpoint; select grok-4.7, grok-4.6, or grok-4.5 explicitly where they are available. xAI does not currently expose a public embeddings or moderation API, so those defaults fall back to OpenAI when xAI is selected. Explicit provider IDs in your config still take precedence.

## Supported Models

The xAI provider includes support for the following model formats. xAI recommendsgrok-4.7 for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work; consult the public model catalog for current availability.

Legacy xAI model aliases

xAI periodically retires older model slugs and keeps them working through redirects. As of the May 15, 2026 (12:00 PM PT) retirement, requests to thegrok-4-1-fast, grok-4-fast, grok-4-0709, and grok-3 families redirect to grok-4.3 and use Grok 4.3 pricing. Requests to grok-code-fast-1 route to grok-build-0.1, while grok-imagine-image-pro routes to grok-imagine-image-quality. For new configs, use a current canonical model ID directly.

Regional model availability

xAI documents Grok 4.7 on its global and US regional endpoints, and announced Grok 4.5 availability in the EU API Console. Check your account before depending on Grok 4.7 in another region;grok-4.3 remains Promptfoo's automatic fallback.

### Grok 4.7 Models

- xai:grok-4.7 - Chat Completions; 500K context, text and image input, text output
- xai:responses:grok-4.7 - Responses API, including server-side tools and encrypted reasoning

Use the exactgrok-4.7 model ID. Grok 4.7 Fast is available in Cursor and Grok Build, but not on the public xAI API.

### Grok 4.6 Models

- xai:grok-4.6 - Previous flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)

xAI does not publish any aliases for this model, so target the exactgrok-4.6 id. There is no grok-4.6-latest.

### Grok 4.5 Models

- xai:grok-4.5 - Flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)
- xai:grok-4.5-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family
- xai:grok-build-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family

### Grok 4.3 Models

- xai:grok-4.3 - General-purpose reasoning model
- xai:grok-4.3-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.3 family
- xai:grok-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.3 family

### Grok 4.20 Models

- xai:grok-4.20-0309-reasoning - Reasoning model
- xai:grok-4.20 - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-reasoning - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-reasoning-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning - Non-reasoning variant
- xai:grok-4.20-non-reasoning - Alias for the Grok 4.20 non-reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-non-reasoning-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 non-reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 - Multi-agent variant
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent - Alias for the Grok 4.20 multi-agent family
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 multi-agent family

### Grok 4.1 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-1-fast-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok Code Fast Models

- xai:grok-build-0.1 - Canonical Grok Build coding model (256K context)
- xai:grok-code-fast-1 - Legacy alias that routes to grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast - Alias for grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast-1-0825 - Versioned alias for grok-build-0.1

### Grok-4 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-fast-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-fast-non-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok-4 Models

- xai:grok-4-0709, xai:grok-4, and xai:grok-4-latest - Legacy IDs that redirect to Grok 4.3 with low reasoning effort

### Grok-3 Models

Thegrok-3, grok-3-beta, grok-3-fast, and related -latest IDs are legacy aliases that redirect to Grok 4.3. Promptfoo also recognizes the older Grok 3 Mini IDs for backward compatibility; verify their availability for your xAI account before relying on them.

### Grok-2 and previous Models

Promptfoo recognizes oldergrok-2, grok-beta, and vision IDs for existing configs, but they are not in xAI's current public catalog. Use a current model for new configs and verify legacy availability in the xAI Console.

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI-compatible configuration options plus Grok-specific options, subject to the model restrictions below. Example usage:

When xAI returnsusage.cost_in_usd_ticks, Promptfoo uses that exact billed amount, including cache discounts and request-level pricing adjustments. If ticks are unavailable, Promptfoo falls back to the model's catalog rates and applies the documented 2x premium when the response confirms service_tier: priority. Custom pricing can be set with cost, inputCost, outputCost, and cacheReadCost (all per-token rates); explicit overrides take precedence over reported ticks and are used as final rates without an additional priority multiplier.
providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.7
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      reasoning_effort: 'xhigh' # low, medium, high (default), or xhigh
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to XAI_API_KEY

Bothxai:<model> Chat Completions and xai:responses:<model> support xAI
Priority Processing.
Set service_tier to priority for higher scheduling priority or default for standard
processing; omitting it also uses the default tier. Other OpenAI-compatible tier names are not
valid on xAI.

### Reasoning Support

Multiple Grok models support reasoning capabilities:

Grok 4.7 and 4.6: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, high (the default), or xhigh. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort. Reasoning cannot be disabled; Promptfoo rejects none locally.

For Grok 4.7, cap output withmax_completion_tokens for Chat Completions or max_output_tokens for Responses. Chat also accepts max_tokens as an alias; use one spelling throughout an eval, including defaults and test cases. Within test options, set a request option directly or under passthrough, not both. Reasoning effort accepts a direct eval variable such as {{ effort }}; see the optional Grok 4.7 providers in the xAI chat example.

Grok 4.5: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, or high (the default); Promptfoo rejects other values locally. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort with the same values.

Grok 4.3: General-purpose reasoning model. Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high; Responses API requests use reasoning.effort.

Grok Code Fast Models: Thegrok-code-fast-1 family are reasoning models optimized for agentic coding workflows. They support:

- Function calling and tool usage
- Web search viasearch_parameters
- Fast inference with built-in reasoning

### Grok 4.7 Specific Behavior

The xAI release notes list $2/M input, $0.50/M cached input, and $6/M output. At 200K or more input tokens, the rates are $4/M, $1/M, and $12/M respectively. When the API does not return a billed cost, Promptfoo uses these rates, including the 10% premium on xAI's US endpoint; explicit custom rates still take precedence. As with other Grok 4 reasoning models, Promptfoo stripspresence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop.

The Responses API returns encrypted reasoning even wheninclude is omitted. Promptfoo keeps it in response.raw.output; pass these items back unchanged when managing conversation history yourself.

### Grok 4.5 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.5 is an earlier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work:

- 500K context window with text and image input
- Configurable reasoning:reasoning_effort accepts low, medium, or high (defaults to high); none is rejected
- Long-context pricing: requests with at least 200K input tokens use the higher catalog rate ($4/M input, $0.60/M cached input, and $12/M output instead of $2/M, $0.30/M, and $6/M); Promptfoo uses the exact billed ticks when xAI returns them
- Unsupported parameters:presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop are rejected, and Promptfoo strips them automatically
- Ignored parameters: xAI silently ignoreslogprobs and top_logprobs on Grok 4.20 and newer models
- Server-side tools: usexai:responses:grok-4.5 for web search, X search, code execution, and MCP

providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.5
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      reasoning_effort: medium
      max_completion_tokens: 4096

### Grok 4.3 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.3 is a general-purpose alternative for text workflows:

- Responses API recommended: Usexai:responses:grok-4.3 for server-side tools, multi-turn state, and newer xAI capabilities
- Configurable reasoning: Setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high
- Unsupported parameters: Same restrictions as other Grok 4-family reasoning models (presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop)

providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.3
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      max_completion_tokens: 4096

Grok-3 Models: Promptfoo retains the legacy Grok 3 Mini reasoning-effort contract for backward compatibility. Use Grok 4.3 or Grok 4.7 for new configurations.

### Grok 4.1 Fast Specific Behavior

These retired IDs redirect to Grok 4.3 but retain their legacy request contract. Promptfoo stripsreasoning_effort, presence_penalty, freque

# Amid Anthropic’s IPO, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI Drop New AI Models

With the focus on Nvidia and Anthropic, several new models were released by OpenAI and Microsoft.

Katelyn is a reporter with CNET covering artificial intelligence, including chatbots, image and video generators.… Read full bio

It’s been a wild week for the AI industry — and it’s only Thursday. Aside from outages, cheating scandals and Anthropic’s pending IPO, there are several new models available now. Google dropped Gemini 4 Neon, Microsoft dropped seven new versions of its MAI models at its Ignite conference, and OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, the next step forward for its flagship models.

First, Google: The tech titan dropped Gemini 4 Neon, its latest flagship model. Besides continuing its trend of naming the Gemini 4 family of models after elements from the periodic table, Gemini 4 Neon boasts better speeds for complex tasks and scientific work. It’s available now for paying Google AI subscribers and developers.

Next, Microsoft: At its Ignite developer conference on Tuesday, Microsoft introduced seven new AI models. They include MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Code 2, MAI Image 2.7 and Dragon Copilot Transcribe — models meant to help with tasks in cybersecurity, coding, image generation and transcription.

More from CNET

It’s clear from Microsoft’s marketing that it is aiming to position its new tech as a cheaper alternative to OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s leading models, with many of these significantly cheaper to run at the enterprise level. That, plus its new licensed weight program, which lets companies customize the new AI models for their purposes, highlights how Microsoft is continuing to pitch its AI tech to the workplace.

And let’s not forget OpenAI: The ChatGPT maker dropped two new model variants of its flagship model, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Astra is the big model — it costs the most and uses the most firepower to handle complex tasks — and Sol is the “everyday” version. Both models beat their sibling models in OpenAI’s benchmarking. These are available to paying subscribers in ChatGPT and Codex globally now. (Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

## The AI elephant in the room

While these new models might be useful for AI power users, they are far from most of the AI industry’s mind this week. During Tuesday’s earnings call, new interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress tried to assure investors that everything was “business as usual” after weeks of turmoil inside the company rocked the global economy. Nvidia cofounder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang’s multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, threw the company into chaos and have attracted the attention of the Securities and Exchange Commission and both chambers of Congress, where Huang has agreed to testify.

And then there’s Anthropic. The Claude maker is becoming a public company this week, with the possible biggest-ever IPO. Anthropic had an opening price of $83 per share, valuing it at $1.5 trillion — narrowly surpassing the valuation of Elon Musk’s mega-conglomerate, SpaceX, at its record-setting IPO earlier this year (now with SpaceXSI, because President Donald Trump said so).

The Nvidia scandal caused a drastic 14% dip in its stock price during its first week and wiped out $1 trillion in the company’s value, but Anthropic investors don’t seem to be worried. At least, not publicly.

If nothing else, Anthropic’s IPO and the new models from Google, OpenAI and Microsoft are stark reminders that the tech industry is nowhere near ready to slow down on AI. Even as financial, environmental and legal concerns mount — and arguably hit a fever pitch during the midterm elections — Big Tech is plowing ahead with generative AI.

# Model Release Notes

Review OpenAI model releases, capability updates, retirements, and changes to the Model Spec.

# November 17, 2026

## GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in the OpenAI API

We’re introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in the OpenAI API. Astra is our frontier model for applications that need advanced reasoning, coding, and the ability to handle complex professional work. Sol combines speed and lower cost with the ability to work through tasks that take several steps. Both improve on their predecessors’ results on demanding tasks while generating fewer output tokens.
Use gpt-6.2-astra or gpt-6.2-sol with the Responses or Chat Completions API. Both models accept text and images and return text, and review Standard API rates.

# November 16, 2026

## OpenAI CSAM image classifier

The OpenAI CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material) Image Classifier helps approved organizations review images for potential CSAM, including AI-generated material. Access is available through the OpenAI API at no cost and requires approval.

The classifier returns scores that can help trained reviewers prioritize review. It does not replace human judgment. Organizations remain responsible for reviewing results and deciding what action to take, including any reporting obligations.

Access requires an application, verification, program onboarding, and acceptance of the applicable terms. For application instructions, see: Requesting access to the OpenAI CSAM Image Classifier.

# October 30, 2026

## GPT-6 Rosalind Research

GPT-6 Rosalind Research brings GPT-6 reasoning capabilities to multistep life sciences research, with safeguards designed for biological work. It is rolling out to a limited set of approved Research customers in Work, Codex, and the API. It is not available in the Chat tab.

Access requires Rosalind Research approval for your organization and authorized users. Discovery approval does not grant Research access. Customers can continue to use GPT-5.5 Rosalind Research, and Rosalind Discovery remains on 5.5. On the API, usegpt-6-rosalind.

In Enterprise workspaces, the model starts in a two-week Admin Preview and is off by default. Admins can enable approved Research users and configure access for after the preview.

For access and setup, see: GPT-Rosalind for life sciences research. For pricing, see: API pricing, the credit-based rate card, or the Enterprise token-based rate card.

# October 29, 2026

## GPT-6 in ChatGPT update

We’re updating GPT-6 in Chat to give more concise responses and reduce overly flattering language. This update applies to Free and Go users, and people using ChatGPT without signing in.

On Plus and Pro, it applies only to the model ChatGPT can switch to after you reach GPT-6 message limits. The main GPT-6 model on Plus and Pro is unchanged.

## Updates to the OpenAI Model Spec

We’ve updated the Model Spec, our public description of how we want our models to behave. The revision reorganizes its guidance around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. It clarifies how GPT should understand human intent and exercise judgment in unfamiliar situations while remaining faithful to human direction and oversight.

Alongside clearer explanations of existing principles, the update adds guidance on context, memory, personalization, human agency, and oversight, and revises guidance on controlling and communicating side effects. It also adjusts some behavioral defaults and retires most detailed style guidance. Throughout the Spec, we now refer to the model as “GPT” rather than “the assistant,” reflecting its broader range of uses.

Read more about the changes and their rationale in our blog post, or explore the updated Model Spec.

# October 26, 2026

## GPT-6.1 Terra

GPT-6.1 Terra is rolling out in the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-terra and in ChatGPT Work and Codex. It supports a range of tasks, including visual reasoning, computer use, and writing.

Standard API pricing is $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens. API usage is billed separately from ChatGPT subscriptions.

In ChatGPT, Terra is available in Work and Codex, not Chat. It does not support UAE inference residency; this restriction is based on where inference runs, not your location.

For API capabilities and availability, see: Model directory. For help choosing a model in Work or Codex, see: Models.

# October 14, 2026

## Retiring GPT-5.5

We’re retiring GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. This change does not affect API access.

# August 18, 2026

## Updates to the OpenAI Model Spec

We’ve updated the Model Spec, our living document outlining intended model behavior.

This update adds additional clarity around principles on appropriate relational interactions for teens. It also clarifies how assistants should handle false or unsupported premises, removes outdated guidance for pre-reasoning models, adds a new section "Be clear about capabilities and limits", and makes a few other small changes and copy edits.

More information on our principles related to teens can be found in our ChatGPT for Teens blog post, and the latest version of the Model Spec is available at model-spec.openai.com.

# July 9, 2026

## Introducing GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT

We’re beginning the rollout of GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT, our flagship reasoning model for complex work across coding, research, science, cybersecurity, computer use, and design.

GPT-5.6 Sol is rolling out to eligible paid ChatGPT plans. Free, Go, and logged-out users are not included. Availability may vary during rollout, and managed-workspace access can depend on administrator settings. Availability for other GPT-5.6 family models varies by product and plan; check the model picker or current rate card in the product you use.

# May 28, 2026

## GPT-5.5 Instant Update

We’re updating GPT-5.5 Instant in ChatGPT and the API to improve response style and quality. It’s now easier to read, more natural in everyday conversations, and better paced in practical help tasks, with fewer overly long or bullet-heavy responses.

With this update, canvas will no longer be available in GPT-5.5 Instant or GPT-5.5 Thinking. Writing and coding functionality is now supported directly in chat responses through writing blocks and code blocks. Paid users can continue using canvas for a limited time through legacy models until those models are sunset.

## Retiring OpenAI o3 and GPT-4.5

Today, we’re continuing to retire older models with limited usage in ChatGPT so we can better serve our newer, most capable models. OpenAI o3 will be retired from ChatGPT on August 26, 2026 following a 90-day sunset period, and GPT-4.5 will be retired from ChatGPT on June 27, 2026 following a 30-day sunset period. These models are currently available to paid users only via model settings. These changes apply to ChatGPT only; there are no changes to the API.

# March 18, 2026

## GPT-5.4 mini in ChatGPT

We’re rolling out GPT-5.4 mini in ChatGPT. GPT-5.4 mini is available to Free and Go users via the “Thinking” feature in the + menu. For all other users, GPT-5.4 mini is available as a rate limit fallback for GPT-5.4 Thinking.

For Plus, Pro, and other paid users, GPT-5.4 mini will be used as a fallback for GPT-5.4 Thinking when rate limits are reached, helping with continued access to reasoning capabilities during high usage. Enterprise customers will retain the option to default Auto routing to GPT-5.4 mini, if preferred.

GPT-5.4 mini will not appear as a selectable model in the model picker, and GPT-5 Thinking mini will be retired as a selectable option in 30 days. Learn more in our blog post.

# March 16, 2026

## GPT-5.3 Instant update

We’re rolling out an update to GPT-5.3 Instant that improves follow-up tone and reduces teaser-style phrasing in responses (e.g., “If you want…”, “You’ll never believe…”, “I can tell you these three things that…”).

# March 11, 2026

## Retiring GPT-5.1 models

As of March 11, 2026, GPT-5.1 models are no longer available in ChatGPT.

This applies to GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, and GPT-5.1 Pro. Existing conversations that used GPT-5.1 will automatically continue on the corresponding current model: GPT-5.3 Instant, GPT-5.4 Thinking, or GPT-5.4 Pro.

# March 5, 2026

## GPT-5.4 Thinking in ChatGPT

GPT‑5.4 brings together the best of our recent advances in reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows into a single frontier model. It incorporates the industry-leading coding capabilities of GPT‑5.3‑Codex while improving how the model works across tools, software environments, and professional tasks involving spreadsheets, presentations, and documents. The result is a model that gets complex real work done accurately, effectively, and efficiently—delivering what you asked for with less back and forth.

In ChatGPT, GPT‑5.4 Thinking can now provide an upfront plan of its thinking, so you can adjust course mid-response while it’s working, and arrive at a final output that’s more closely aligned with what you need without additional turns. GPT‑5.4 Thinking improves deep web research, particularly for highly specific queries, while better maintaining context for questions that require longer thinking. GPT‑5.4 Thinking also has improved context window management that supports its ability to think for longer. Together, these improvements mean higher-quality answers that arrive faster and stay relevant to the task at hand.

GPT‑5.3 Instant delivers more accurate answers, richer and better-contextualized results when searching the web, and reduces unnecessary dead ends, caveats, and overly declarative phrasing that can interrupt the flow of conversation.

# Alibaba Launches Qwen4-Max AI Model With Focus on Security

The 2.4-trillion-parameter model includes a 1-million-token context window, native vision capabilities and security improvements across coding and other tasks.

## Key takeaways

- Alibaba has launched the Qwen4-Max AI model, featuring 2.4 trillion parameters and a 1-million-token context window.
- The model is designed for a wide range of applications, including 3D modelling, finance, and healthcare.
- Qwen4-Max outperforms its predecessor, Qwen3.8-Max, in nearly every evaluated capability, with reduced token usage.

Alibaba has introduced Qwen4-Max, its latest flagship artificial intelligence (AI) model. Built on a new architecture with 2.4 trillion parameters and a 1-million-token context window, the model is designed for complex professional and scientific tasks.

“It can take on a wide range of creative and professional work,” Alibaba said, citing applications in 3D modelling, game development, precision manufacturing, finance, law, healthcare, and scientific discovery.

Qwen4-Max succeeds Qwen3.8-Max, which Alibaba launched in August. The company said the new model outperforms its predecessor across nearly every evaluated capability. In its Work360 evaluation, token usage fell by approximately 24% and 35% at Xhigh and High effort levels, respectively, the company claimed.

Alibaba also reduced API prices, particularly for cached inputs. The average cost per task in its Work360 evaluation fell from $4.43 to $1.67—a 62% reduction. The earlier Qwen3.8-Max launch marked another step in Alibaba's expansion of its AI model portfolio.

The company also highlighted improvements in security testing. On Last Secure Code Bench, Qwen4-Max's function-level pass rate for both functionality and security increased from 22% for Qwen3.8-Max to 31.8%. The share of code meeting security requirements at the function, file, and repository levels rose from 8% to 14.7%.

Alibaba said it had strengthened safeguards against cybersecurity misuse by retaining training data for defensive tasks, such as vulnerability detection and remediation, while removing data intended to improve offensive attack capabilities. Internal testing found no capabilities posing large-scale cybersecurity risks.

For chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risks, Alibaba introduced dedicated safety data during post-training. The company said internal evaluations found that the model identified more potentially harmful requests and provided safe responses, without significantly increasing users' ability to carry out harmful tasks.

AI Compass

### Why AI Needs a Different Kind of Cloud
Read on AI Compass 
The security focus comes after scrutiny of earlier Qwen models. A Cohere security evaluation of an Alibaba Qwen model raised concerns about the model's behaviour during testing.

Alibaba's latest release comes amid growing competition among Chinese technology companies to improve AI model performance while reducing operating costs. Several Chinese developers have also gained prominence in the global open-weight AI market.

Qwen4-Max is available through Alibaba's QwenCloud platform, QwenWork, Qoder, and QwenStudio. Developers can access it through a token plan or API.

cross_cutting.content:
# Microsoft Copilot Autopilot Launches With Agent Identity

Microsoft officially launched Copilot Autopilot on November 18, 2026, introducing the first always-on autonomous AI agent with its own Microsoft Entra identity. Announced by Chief Marketing Officer Jared Spataro at the Microsoft Ignite keynote in San Francisco, the platform represents a fundamental architectural shift in how enterprise AI agents authenticate, operate, and audit their actions across Microsoft 365 environments.

## Autopilot Agent Gets Dedicated Authentication

Copilot Autopilot operates as a fully autonomous entity with its own login credentials, memory systems, and productivity tool ecosystem. Unlike previous assistants that act on behalf of human users, Autopilot authenticates under its own Microsoft Entra identity. This architecture change means every action the agent takes logs under its own name rather than impersonating a user, creating clear audit trails for security teams.

The agent monitors Teams channels and email inboxes continuously, automating recurring workflows without human intervention. Autopilot ships through Microsoft's Frontier early-access program rather than general availability, indicating the company is testing deployment patterns with select enterprise customers first.

## WorkIQ Coordinates 19.5 Exabytes of Data

Underpinning the new agent architecture is WorkIQ, described by Spataro as the centralized reasoning layer for all Copilot agents. WorkIQ retrieves data, interprets intent, and prioritizes information across the roughly 19.5 exabytes of customer business data stored in Microsoft 365 today. With billions of new files, documents, emails, and messages added daily, WorkIQ provides the intelligence infrastructure that lets multiple agents coordinate actions without conflicting.

This reasoning layer marks Microsoft's answer to the orchestration challenge facing multi-agent systems. Rather than each agent operating in isolation, WorkIQ creates a shared context that all Copilot variants can reference when making decisions or taking actions.

## 100+ Prebuilt Skills and Salesforce Partnership

Microsoft is bundling substantial prebuilt functionality into the Copilot ecosystem. Dynamics 365 in Copilot ships with more than 100 prebuilt skills covering sales, service, and finance workflows. These skills let agents execute common business processes without custom development.

A new Salesforce partnership called Copilotforce adds 38 CRM-focused skills, paired with Zero Copy two-way integration between Microsoft Fabric and Salesforce Data 360. The integration lets data flow between the two platforms without duplication, addressing a long-standing friction point for enterprises running hybrid Microsoft-Salesforce stacks.

Additional developer tools include Copilot Managed Runtime for hosting AI-generated applications and Copilot Code, a dashboard and widget generator launching in the next few weeks. Agent 365 adds Business Analytics for FinOps-style budgeting of agent computational spend, acknowledging that autonomous agents create new cost management requirements.

## Release Date and Availability

Officially launched on November 18, 2026, Copilot Autopilot and Copilot Workspaces are available through Microsoft's Frontier early-access program. Copilot Home, Office in Copilot (the full Office suite integrated into the Copilot app), and Managed Runtime reached general availability on the same date. The staggered rollout suggests Microsoft is managing risk on the most autonomous features while making productivity enhancements broadly available.

## What This Means for Enterprise AI

Microsoft's decision to give AI agents dedicated identities solves critical compliance and security challenges that have slowed enterprise adoption of autonomous systems. With Autopilot actions logged under the agent's own account, IT teams can audit AI decisions separately from human activity. The WorkIQ reasoning layer and prebuilt skill libraries lower the technical barrier for deploying multi-agent workflows, potentially accelerating enterprise migration from assisted AI to fully autonomous business processes. This launch positions Microsoft as the first major platform vendor to ship production-grade agent identity infrastructure at scale.

About the writer

Sarvesh is a Product Manager at Emergent, focused on building AI-powered products that help people turn ideas into software.

# AI agents are coming to help hire, schedule, and manage frontline workers as Fountain launches Orchestra

A manager trying to cover a vacant shift or revive an unanswered job application does not need another dashboard showing that work has stalled. The immediate need is someone—or something—to complete the follow-up.

Fountain, a 12-year-old San Francisco–based software company that helps employers hire and manage hourly frontline workers, is making that the premise of Orchestra, an AI agent builder for firms with large, hourly workforces.

Teams describe an assignment or business objective, approve the agent's proposed design, and let it carry out recurring recruiting and staffing tasks using information already in Fountain.

Orchestra is a proprietary service available at launch at no charge to selected existing customers inside their Fountain accounts.

Fountain, whose broader platform serves more than 500 frontline employers, says general availability is planned for early 2027. At that point, customers will pay for the work agents do and be able to limit how much work they take on. Prospective buyers can contact the company through Fountain's website.

In a November 9 post about Fountain's pricing model, chief product and technology officer Salim Jernite said credits cost 50 cents, with charges tied to completed outcomes and no charge for failed attempts.

He also described budgets for individual agents and accounts, advance cost estimates for large or unusual runs, and automatic pauses when spending looks unusual. The launch release gives no Orchestra rate card, leaving buyers without a confirmed price for outcomes such as a filled shift.

Jernite said in an exclusive interview with VentureBeat that about six customers were using Orchestra when he spoke ahead of launch.

## From a requested answer to an ongoing assignment

Orchestra builds on Cue, the AI tool Fountain launched in April 2026. Fountain says customers have asked Cue more than 80,000 questions since launch. With Orchestra, customers can set up agents to handle recurring work or act when an event occurs.

Agents can reconnect with past applicants, prepare new hires for their first day or respond when a position opens. Teams can run an agent on demand or on a schedule, or have it start when a specific event occurs.

Jernite described how the shift coverage example would work. A worker dropping a shift could trigger an agent to check the roster, factor in overtime and contact preferences, and reach out to eligible workers.

“It’s going to call them until it reaches one that actually accepts the shift,” he told VentureBeat. The agent would then assign the shift and text the manager.

The setup process includes a human approval step. Jernite described three ways to start. A user can specify what an agent should do, describe a problem such as applicants stalling at a particular stage, or ask Orchestra to review operations and suggest where agents could help.

In the second case, the system might propose texting or calling an applicant after two days of inactivity. Orchestra presents a design for review before creating it, and Jernite said it can show customers how a proposed agent performs in simulations. Agents can serve a team without being assigned separately to every employee.

Fountain already offers preconfigured agents for tasks such as interviewing candidates and surveying employees. Jernite said Orchestra grew out of customers’ need to adapt automation to their own systems and processes. He expects corporate recruiting and operations teams to build agents that handle work for managers in the field. He pointed to the staff who coordinate hiring, onboarding and shift coverage. “This is the layer that we’re optimizing with agents,” he said.

The distinction matters for organizations deciding whether to purchase a workforce application or build similar automation themselves. A general agent can generate messages and call tools, but it still needs access to the right employee records, application status, scheduling information and permissions. Fountain's proposition is that much of that operational context already resides in its product.

## How Fountain builds agents and connects outside tools

Fountain built the software that manages agent instructions, tools and memory, along with the records it keeps for messaging and consent, Jernite said.

The system primarily uses Anthropic’s Claude models. Jernite said Orchestra uses Opus 5.5 to design agents, most of the resulting agents run on Sonnet 5.5, and smaller agents can use Haiku for jobs such as reading logs and maintaining memory.

“We adapt the model depending on the complexity of the tasks,” he said. Customer-built agents can also assign work to other agents so they can carry out several actions in parallel.

The builder can suggest connecting outside tools through the Model Context Protocol, or MCP, Jernite said. “You could create agents anywhere else. You can actually bring them to Orchestra,” he said.

He described a Microsoft 365 integration that lets Orchestra call Microsoft Copilot agents to handle parts of an assignment. Orchestra itself runs within Fountain, and Jernite’s account of importing agents left open whether customers can swap out the models that Fountain uses to build and run its own agents.

## Checking whether the agent actually finished

Fountain says the agent sets a plan and an objective each time it runs. A separate check reviews the actions the agent took against that objective before marking the work complete. When the work falls short, the system flags it for a person to review and explains why.

“Knowing when it hasn’t completed the job and why is the hard part,” Jernite said in the announcement.

“Each agent that is created on Orchestra has a goal and is checked against that goal,” Jernite told VentureBeat. He said the goal specifies a successful outcome and sets limits on what the agent may do to achieve it. A separate AI agent checks whether the goal was met in full or in part and can recommend up to three reruns.

The check is a significant part of the product's pitch. An agent that reports success after sending a message has not necessarily secured coverage for an open shift. Evaluating completed work requires a definition of success tied to the underlying business record, not merely the agent's own explanation.

Fountain says it uses more than 180 agents internally across functions including engineering, finance and customer-facing operations. The launch release provides no independent evaluation or customer performance figures for Orchestra.

## Permissions and outreach controls are part of the design

According to Fountain, agents inherit the permissions of the person running them. On each call to an applicant or worker, the system checks consent, allowed calling hours and daily contact limits. It identifies itself as AI and honors opt-outs.

The company also says outreach follows predefined objective criteria, discriminatory instructions are refused, and people retain hiring decisions. Agent activity is recorded in readable language.

Those are product claims, not proof that every configured workflow will behave correctly. A buyer evaluating Orchestra would still need to test whether the permission boundary holds in practice, how failed checks reach a person and what information remains in an audit record.

## Workday and Microsoft offer different routes to similar automation

Orchestra sits between specialized recruiting automation and general-purpose agent-building software.

Workday's Paradox candidate-experience offering already supports conversational applications, candidate questions and interview scheduling, with connections to applicant-tracking systems. It is a direct comparison for employers focused on recruiting throughput. Workday's public product page routes buyers to sales rather than providing a dollar rate card.

Microsoft Copilot Studio offers a broader toolkit for building agents across business processes. Its published pricing includes a $200 monthly capacity pack with 25,000 Copilot Credits, alongside other purchasing options. Those credits measure Microsoft's service consumption, while Fountain proposes charging for completed work.

# Genesys Launches Standalone AI Agents and Genesys Arena for Faster Agentic AI Deployment

New effort-based pricing lets customers pay based on the work required to complete each task, with consumption measured in Experience Units

SAN FRANCISCO, November 17, 2026 –– Genesys®, a global leader in agentic orchestration for customer experience (CX), today announced Genesys Standalone AI Agents and Genesys Arena to help enterprises scale agentic AI faster and with greater flexibility. Genesys Standalone AI Agents will allow organizations to begin their agentic transformation within their existing customer service environments, while Genesys Arena complements the offering to help teams turn proven CX use cases into production-ready AI agents.

“Enterprises want to move faster with AI, but they need the flexibility to do it on their own terms without compromising trust and governance,” said Tony Bates, chairman and CEO of Genesys. “With Standalone AI Agents, Genesys Arena and a new effort-based pricing model, we’re giving organizations more choice in how they put agentic AI to work today and scale it as their needs evolve.”

An Entry Point to Agentic AI for Existing Customer Service Environments

Genesys Standalone AI Agents provide organizations a way to deploy Genesys Cloud™ Agentic Virtual Agent without first migrating their broader customer service environment to Genesys Cloud. Organizations can put AI agents into production in a few days while preserving existing technology investments, workflows and operations.

The offering lets enterprises introduce agentic AI into customer service while keeping broader transformation decisions on their own timeline. Organizations can start with a specific task and use Genesys Standalone AI Agents to handle customer requests within defined business rules and guardrails. If an issue requires human expertise, the AI agent can pass the conversation and its context to an employee so the customer doesn’t have to start over.

From Use Case to Functional AI Agents in Minutes

Genesys Arena offers organizations a quicker path to deploying AI agents with prebuilt Agent Kits designed for proven, industry-specific customer experience use cases. Each kit provides a working model with the knowledge, skills, integrations and guardrails teams need, eliminating the need to build foundational components from scratch.

With Agent Kits spanning more than 50 common industry use cases, teams can create a functional AI agent in as little as 10 minutes, customize it using natural language, preview the experience and deploy it directly into Genesys Cloud. Organizations can then tailor each agent to meet their specific customer, business and regulatory requirements.

“AI is advancing quickly, and enterprises shouldn’t have to start from zero every time they want to put a new idea to work,” said Youssef Nokta, senior vice president of AI forward deployed engineering at Genesys. “Genesys Arena gives teams a practical head start, so they can spend less time on the foundational work and more time shaping AI around their customers, business and the results they want to achieve.”

The Right Persona for Every Customer Experience

Voice customization tools coming to Arena and the Genesys Cloud platform will grant organizations control over how their Genesys Cloud Agentic Virtual Agents represent their brand across different customer experiences. Builders can start with a recommended persona for a specific use case; customize its personality, tone and delivery using natural language; then preview and deploy it directly to Genesys Cloud. Organizations can create distinct personas for different roles and interactions while maintaining consistency with their brand.

“Using Genesys Agentic Virtual Agent has shown us how AI can improve the customer experience and drive efficiency by resolving more interactions autonomously,” said Michael Buttsworth, associate director, student experience service center at Charles Sturt University. “Getting that value into production depends on how quickly teams can move from an idea to an experience that works in the real world. Genesys Arena and Agent Kits will make that path easier by giving organizations a more accessible starting point for building and tailoring agentic experiences to their customers, operations and brand.”

More Flexible Pricing Based on the Work AI Performs

Genesys is also introducing effort-based pricing for greater flexibility as enterprises scale AI adoption. The model aligns cost with the work performed by classifying interactions as simple, moderate or complex, so customers pay less for straightforward tasks. Usage is measured in Experience Units, with each interaction counted once and assigned a pricing tier based on the tools required to complete it.

Genesys is renaming AI Tokens to Experience Units to reflect a broader shift from paying for AI technology to measuring the work performed and experiences delivered. Experience Units provide a common way to consume Genesys Cloud AI products while aligning investment more closely with customer experience outcomes and business value.

“Enterprises are under pressure to move agentic AI from experimentation into production quickly, but they aren’t all starting from the same place. Some are operating in the cloud while others are navigating complex hybrid or on-premises environments,” said Mila D’Antonio, principal analyst, customer engagement at Omdia. “Genesys Arena and Genesys Standalone AI Agents give organizations different paths to deploy agentic AI based on their existing environment and requirements. The introduction of effort-based pricing also highlights how commercial models are evolving as organizations consider how to adopt and scale agentic AI.”

Genesys Standalone AI Agents are generally available now. Genesys Agent Kits will be generally available through Genesys Arena later this month. To learn more about the newest offerings, visit www.genesys.com/ai.

Forward-Looking Statements

Statements in this press release that are not historical or current facts are forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Unless required by law, Genesys undertakes no obligation to update or revise any forward-looking statements to reflect circumstances or events after the date of this press release.

About Genesys

Genesys® empowers more than 8,000 organizations worldwide to create the best customer and employee experiences. Genesys Cloud™ is the Agentic Orchestration Platform that securely connects people, systems, data and AI across the enterprise with built-in governance and control. As a result, organizations can drive customer loyalty, growth and retention while increasing operational efficiency and teamwork across human and AI workforces. To learn more, visit www.genesys.ai.

cross_cutting.content:

# Eightfold launches AI Recruiting Teammate for hiring teams
Wed, 18th Nov 2026 (Today) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

Eightfold AI has launched AI Recruiting Teammate for recruiting teams, aiming to reduce the need for recruiters to manage multiple AI tools.

The software targets organisations that use separate systems for tasks such as sourcing, screening and scheduling, bringing those steps into a single, goal-based workflow. Recruiters can describe a hiring objective in plain language, and the system manages actions across open requisitions while leaving final decisions to recruiters and hiring managers.

The launch comes as HR technology suppliers add more AI products to automate parts of the hiring process. Eightfold is positioning the product as an alternative to using several disconnected agents across different stages of recruitment.

According to Eightfold, the product is designed to cover the hiring process from intake to onboarding. It can calibrate a role, identify candidates, coordinate outreach, arrange screening interviews and continue follow-up over days or weeks, while allowing recruiters to pause, redirect or take over the process.

Joe Korngiebel, Chief Executive Officer of Eightfold AI, said the problem for recruiters is not a lack of automation but the burden of managing too many tools.

"With AI so rapidly reshaping work, recruiters need AI agents that work alongside them, not more agents to manage. AI Recruiting Teammate frees recruiters to spend more time making the hiring decisions that matter, from intake to onboarding, while keeping workflows moving across sourcing, scheduling and candidate follow-up," Korngiebel said.

The system draws on Eightfold's Talent Intelligence platform and uses shared organisational context to coordinate work across recruiting tasks. The company argues that many existing tools automate individual activities but still require recruiters to connect the process manually and move between systems.

Recruiting workflow

The product is intended to act on a hiring goal rather than execute isolated commands. In practice, that means it can continue operating across multiple stages of a requisition without recruiters having to re-enter instructions at each point.

That approach reflects a wider shift in software design, from task-based assistants to systems framed as digital teammates. In recruitment, vendors have increasingly promoted tools that can search candidate pools, draft outreach messages, book interviews and rank applicants. Buyers, however, have also raised concerns about fragmented workflows and oversight.

Eightfold said recruiters remain in control of final hiring decisions and can inspect a record of the system's actions. It added that the product works within organisational boundaries and escalates decisions that require human judgement, along with the evidence behind its recommendations.

AI oversight

The launch also highlights pressure on HR technology companies to show how AI systems are governed. Recruitment software faces close scrutiny because decisions on hiring, screening and matching can affect access to jobs and expose employers to regulatory and reputational risk.

Eightfold said its responsible AI approach includes explainable systems, oversight principles and technical monitoring. This includes regular third-party audits, the company said, and it cited an independent bias audit of its matching model conducted by BABL AI under New York City's Local Law 144.

It also said it has an AI Ethics Council that advises on responsible AI use as regulation develops. Those measures are part of a wider push across the HR software market to reassure employers that automated tools can be used with transparency and review.

Korngiebel's comments also point to a broader debate about where AI fits into white-collar work. Rather than removing recruiters from the process, vendors are increasingly presenting these systems as tools that handle coordination and repetitive administration while people retain authority over judgement-heavy decisions.

For Eightfold, the launch adds to competition in the crowded market for AI hiring tools, where providers are trying to distinguish between simple automation and more autonomous systems. The company said AI Recruiting Teammate is designed to help recruiting teams increase output without adding more standalone agents to their software stack.
