# Insight launches AI agent store for business customers
Thu, 19th Nov 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Insight has launched an online Agent Store for business customers, now generally available in 14 countries.

The store offers a catalogue of AI agents, platforms and related services designed to automate routine work across business functions. Customers can deploy the tools in days or weeks rather than months, either as standalone products or alongside consulting, implementation and managed services.

The launch adds six new agentic products to Insight's AI portfolio, bringing the total in its library to 15. Nine products were introduced earlier this year.

Products listed in the store include Insight AI Flight Academy, focused on training and change management, and TokenScope, which tracks token usage and AI consumption costs for finance teams. Insight said the offerings were first developed for clients or used internally in areas including security, finance and legal.

New products available at launch include Quote Advisor, which assesses pricing, inventory, freight and contract requirements to produce sourced quotes. NDA Review Agent is designed to review non-disclosure agreements against a company's legal policies, while Parts Order Assist helps warehouse, maintenance and field staff search catalogues and place parts orders.

Insight is positioning the store as a way for businesses to move AI projects beyond the pilot stage and into wider use. It said it applied the approach within its own operations before making the products available more broadly.

"Organisations are feeling the pressure to move AI from isolated pilots into production. As 'Client Zero', Insight has built a repeatable approach to help that's been proven first across our own organisation," said Jack Azagury, Chief Executive Officer of Insight.

"Having driven over 90% internal AI adoption, we know firsthand what it takes to deploy and scale agentic AI rapidly and responsibly. By combining the solutions offered in Agent Store with our consulting and managed services expertise, Insight is empowering clients to move from 'hype to how' with AI to deliver measurable results in their own enterprises and generate long-term value across every industry," Azagury said.

Early customer

Culligan International is the first external customer to implement Flight Academy, according to Insight. The water services company is using a mix of AI tools including Microsoft Copilot, Cowork, Copilot Studio, Azure and Microsoft Fabric, while also putting governance in place around cost and responsible use.

The deployment centres on workforce education and internal adoption rather than a single operational use case. Insight said the training-led approach is intended to help organisations build confidence in AI tools across teams and geographies.

"At Culligan, we believe technology doesn't transform a company - people do. Generative AI adoption is far ahead of the learning curve, and it's our responsibility to arm our teams with the best tools to lead now into the future," said Laura Walsh, Global Chief Information Officer of Culligan International.

"With our partners at Insight, we have prioritised AI education so our teams can confidently leverage AI productively and responsibly. We are leveraging Insight's best practice and have established a functional champions network which has turned AI adoption into an organic, community-led effort across functions and geographies," Walsh said.

Geographic reach

Agent Store is available in the United States and Canada, as well as Australia, New Zealand and Singapore. In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, it is available in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom.

The launch reflects growing competition among technology service providers to package AI software, advisory work and operational support into repeatable products that can be rolled out across large organisations. Rather than selling only bespoke AI projects, firms are increasingly assembling catalogues of narrower tools tied to functions such as legal review, quoting, training and cost control.

For customers, that model offers a way to buy more standardised AI products while still relying on outside support for deployment and governance. For providers such as Insight, it creates a route to extend consulting relationships into packaged software and managed services.

Insight's emphasis on internal use before external release also points to a wider market pattern, in which technology companies test automation tools in their own operations before offering them to clients. In this case, Insight said the products had been used across departments to simplify tasks and improve efficiency.

Insight said Agent Store is intended to widen access to automation for core business processes and support broader internal AI adoption, with products spanning legal, finance, operations and employee training.

# Telia joins European technology leaders in forming AI Gigafactory Northern consortium to build trusted, sustainable AI infrastructure

Press release

Telia, Nokia, Nscale, Verda and Skeleton today announce the formation of AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), a European consortium formed to develop trusted, distributed AI infrastructure through a federated, multi-site AI Gigafactory across the Nordic and Baltic region. Operating as a federated AI Gigafactory under European governance, the sites will combine large-scale AI computing infrastructure with sovereign cloud and AI platform services, high-capacity connectivity and decarbonized energy. The partners intend to submit a bid to build and operate AIGF Northern under the call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia published by the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU).

# Telia, Nokia form AI gigafactory alliance

- Telcos are among the players lining up to get involved in Europe’s AI gigafactory plans
- Telia is the latest to show its hand
- It has teamed up with Nokia, neocloud Nscale and others to bid for distributed AI infrastructure deployment funding from the EC

Telia is the latest European telco to throw its hat into the AI gigafactory ring by forming a consortium with Nokia and three others – British neocloud Nscale, Finnish AI cloud provider Verda and Estonian power systems specialist Skeleton Technologies – that will bid for a share of the €10bn funds that the European Commission (EC) is set to pump into seven major AI infrastructure deployments in the European Union.

The move comes as Europe’s major digital infrastructure players decide how, or if, they will get involved with the EC’s plan to help develop sovereign AI infrastructure that will provide the region’s governments and enterprises with a local or regional source for their AI needs.

The EC’s plan revolves around the ‘mobilisation’ of €30bn in investments – up to €10bn from the EC and national public funding sources, and €20bn from the private companies involved in the successful bids. The deadlines for bids to be submitted are fast approaching – 3 December for large-scale facilities and 4 February 2027 for medium-sized facilities – with the winning bids set to be announced in the first half of next year and construction set to commence soon after.

A number of telcos are involved in various bids: Telefónica is heading up a consortium that includes the Spanish government and the Santander banking group; Orange and Iliad Group (via its Scaleway cloud division) are part of the AION consortium; Deutsche Telekom is considering a joint bid with partners but is still wary of the economics associated with the EC’s funding; and Vodafone Group has been linked to a potential bid in partnership with German construction firm Hochtief.

Now Telia has stepped up with its partners to form what they are calling the AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern) consortium, which aims to develop “trusted, distributed AI infrastructure through a federated, multi-site AI gigafactory across the Nordic and Baltic region” that will combine “large-scale AI computing infrastructure with sovereign cloud and AI platform services, high-capacity connectivity and decarbonised energy”.

The consortium members will also be supported by specialist R&D partners, namely the VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, which specialises in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI and photonics, and Sweden’s largest technical university, the KTH Royal Institute of Technology, with which Telia and the telco’s AI infrastructure partner, investment firm Brookfield, recently forged a sovereign AI partnership.

The AIGF Northern consortium plans to distribute capacity across borders to “reduce concentration risk and strengthen the resilience of Europe’s AI ecosystem”. AIGF Northern will connect facilities in: Oulu, Finland; the Tallinn region in Estonia; Valmiera, Latvia; and a to-be-determined location in Sweden.

“Distributing capacity across these locations will allow the consortium to draw on multiple sources of decarbonised energy, expand computing infrastructure where capacity is available and reduce reliance on any single site or supplier. This approach will strengthen operational resilience and support cross-border expansion as European demand for AI grows,” noted the consortium in this announcement.

Telia, together with its systems integration subsidiary Telia Cygate, will “contribute expertise in connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations and sovereign cloud solutions, supporting the development of a federated, multi-country AI ecosystem,” explained the operator.

Anders Olsson, head of Telia Sweden, stated: “Our customers – and our continent – have a rapidly increasing need for scalable and sovereign AI services. To meet this need, Europe’s best must step up. Telia’s highly relevant skills in secure and resilient connectivity and systems integration, combined with our position as a trusted partner for businesses and societies, make us a natural fit for this ambitious consortium. We look forward to working together to create even more value for customers while helping to secure long-term European competitiveness and resilience.”

Taavi Madiberk, CEO and co-founder of Skeleton Technologies, stated: “Europe is stepping up its AI investment, but building lasting AI capacity requires more than compute alone. It also requires the energy and power infrastructure to support that compute efficiently, reliably and at scale, using technologies developed and manufactured in Europe. Northern Europe brings together many of the right conditions: abundant decarbonised electricity, strong engineering capabilities and an advanced industrial base. Skeleton contributes the power systems that ensure AI infrastructure doesn’t waste energy, places less strain on the grid, and gets more compute power from every GPU. The Northern AI Gigafactory is an opportunity to combine these strengths into real European AI capacity, industrial value creation and greater technological sovereignty.”

Mikko Hautala, chief geopolitical and government relations officer at Nokia, added: “Europe’s AI ambitions depend on infrastructure it can trust, control and scale. AIGF Northern brings together the connectivity, computing, cloud and energy capabilities needed to turn that ambition into reality. By linking strengths across borders, we can build a more resilient foundation for European innovation, competitiveness and technological sovereignty.”

- Ray Le Maistre, Editorial Director, TelecomTV

cross_cutting.content:
20-year, 10-megawatt agreement underpins deployment of B300 systems for AI inference

SAN FRANCISCO and NEW YORK, November 17, 2026 — Argentum AI, a premium GPU cloud provider, and Kyndryl (NYSE: KD), a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services, today announced a 20-year, $630M data center collaboration for an initial 10 megawatts (MW) of capacity at Kyndryl’s Boulder, Colorado, facility to power deployment of NVIDIA GPU systems.

Argentum is deploying NVIDIA B300 systems at the site in a fully Tier III environment, creating advanced, enterprise-grade infrastructure to run demanding AI applications at scale. Deployment is underway.

The agreement provides Argentum access to a facility built for the power density of current-generation GPU systems and gives Argentum’s customers a faster path to high-performance inference capacity.

“Partnering with an established technology services and infrastructure provider like Kyndryl is an important milestone for Argentum AI,” said Andrew Sobko, Founder and CEO, Argentum AI. “This agreement reflects our shared commitment to expanding secure, high-performance compute infrastructure and supporting the growing demands of enterprises embracing AI at scale.”

“Our agreement gives us a unique opportunity to put Kyndryl capacity to work in an innovative way, this coupled with our mission-critical capabilities, decades of operational and services experience will support Argentum as it creates capacity for its customers,” said Jamie Rutledge, President, Kyndryl U.S.

The facility welcomes a fast-growing, enterprise-grade AI inference company, whose technology powers some of the world’s most widely used AI applications, as its flagship anchor tenant. Argentum AI and Kyndryl intend to broaden their collaboration to support Argentum’s growth and evolving mission-critical enterprise AI infrastructure needs.

About Argentum AI
Argentum AI is a premium GPU cloud provider. The company originates, finances and operates GPU clusters, delivering dedicated bare metal GPU capacity to AI model builders, inference providers and enterprises. Argentum works with data center operators and builds capacity around customer demand, with a focus on speed of delivery, reliability and long-term partnerships. For more information, visit argentum-ai.com.

About Kyndryl
Kyndryl (NYSE: KD) is a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services, offering advisory, implementation and managed service capabilities to thousands of customers in more than 60 countries. As the world’s largest IT infrastructure services provider, the company designs, builds, manages and modernizes the complex information systems that the world depends on every day. # Nokia, Telia, and Partners Join Forces to Develop Northern European AI Gigafactory

European technology companies Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton Technologies, Telia, and Verda have formed a consortium to develop AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), a federated AI infrastructure project spanning the Nordic and Baltic region. The initiative aims to strengthen Europe’s AI capabilities by combining large-scale computing infrastructure, sovereign cloud services, high-capacity connectivity, and decarbonized energy under European governance.

The founding partners intend to submit a joint bid in response to the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking’s call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia. If selected, the project will connect multiple facilities across Northern Europe, providing businesses, researchers, and public-sector organizations throughout the continent with access to trusted AI computing, cloud, and connectivity services.

The planned infrastructure will span Oulu in Finland, Iru in Estonia, and Valmiera in Latvia, while the location of the Swedish site has yet to be determined. By distributing computing capacity across several countries, the consortium aims to reduce dependence on individual facilities and suppliers, strengthen operational resilience, and support the expansion of Europe’s AI ecosystem.

The project comes as the European Union steps up efforts to develop its own AI infrastructure. Through its InvestAI initiative, the EU aims to mobilize EUR 30 billion in investment, combining EUR 20 billion in private-sector funding with EUR 10 billion from EU and national public sources.

The Nordic and Baltic region offers several advantages for large-scale AI infrastructure, including access to reliable, decarbonized electricity, advanced digital networks, and a cooler climate that can reduce data center cooling requirements. These conditions could help improve energy efficiency and enable facilities to deliver greater computing capacity using existing grid connections.

“Europe’s AI ambitions depend on infrastructure it can trust, control, and scale. AIGF Northern brings together the connectivity, computing, cloud, and energy capabilities needed to turn that ambition into reality. By linking strengths across borders, we can build a more resilient foundation for European innovation, competitiveness, and technological sovereignty,” said Mikko Hautala, Chief Geopolitical and Government Relations Officer and Chairman of Nokia Defense.

Each founding partner will contribute a different part of the infrastructure value chain. Nokia will provide secure, high-performance connectivity and network infrastructure, while Nscale will bring cloud platform capabilities and expertise in AI infrastructure for training and inference. Telia, together with its subsidiary Telia Cygate, will contribute connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations, and cloud solutions. Verda will provide AI-native infrastructure and cloud expertise, while Skeleton Technologies will supply high-power systems designed to improve data center efficiency and stability, reduce pressure on electricity grids, and support lower-carbon operations.

The consortium will also draw on expertise from research and innovation organizations. VTT Technical Research Center of Finland will contribute capabilities in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI, and photonics, while Sweden’s KTH Royal Institute of Technology will support AI research, education, and skills development. Their involvement will connect the infrastructure project with Europe’s wider research, innovation, and talent ecosystems.
